title: Warriors news: Mike Dunleavy Jr. 'lost zero sleep' over Stephen Curry contract
description: SAN FRANCISCO – While uncertainty around Stephen Curry’s future with the Golden State Warriors was as thick and persistent as the San Francisco fog this past summer, general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. never doubted the transformational franchise superstar would end his tenure in the Bay. “I lost zero sleep over that,” Dunleavy said Monday morning at […] The post Warriors news: Mike Dunleavy Jr. 'lost zero sleep' over Stephen Curry contract appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Warriors news: Mike Dunleavy Jr. 'lost zero sleep' over Stephen Curry contract appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

SAN FRANCISCO – While uncertainty around Stephen Curry's future with the Golden State Warriors was as thick and persistent as the San Francisco fog this past summer, general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. never doubted the transformational franchise superstar would end his tenure in the Bay.

"I lost zero sleep over that," Dunleavy said Monday morning at Warriors media day regarding if he worried Curry could set himself to leave Golden State by not signing a contract extension. "He's a guy that's committed to the organization. He wants to be here. He believes in our ability to put together a great team. I've lost sleep on a lot of things. That is not one of them."

Curry put ink to paper to back his commitment, signing a two-year, $116-million extension, with a player option in the second year, which could feasibly keep him with the Warriors till 2029, when he would enter his 20th season with the franchise.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Dunleavy said the Warriors provided Curry several different financial options, giving the future hall of famer the onus to choose whatever path he desired.

"We showed him our books and what it looks like and this and that and the whole thing," Dunleavy explained, saying that he would never ask Curry to take less money. "I think Steph's biggest thing is, allow me to understand. What are we thinking? How are we doing this? So we went through that with him, enabled him some time to give it thought and think about it, and then we came back with this concept that made a ton of sense."

What makes sense about this deal, beyond retaining the man who fills the arena and juices jersey sales, are the team-building possibilities it provides the Golden State. With Curry taking $10 million less annually, the Warriors have a little more flexibility heading into the 2027-28 season with the ability to have north of $60 million available in cap space to pursue a high-level free agent. And while Dunleavy did not provide specifics as to how the Warriors will use that added flexibility, he emphasized that Curry signed the deal that he did with Golden State because he wants to win.

"We found a middle ground where he was incredibly generous in taking this deal, where he's taking less money to help the team out because, as Steph goes, he's as competitive as there is," Dunleavy said. "He wants to win. He's put us in a position where it gives us a little bit more flexibility to do that. So I think the middle ground was signing him up to be able to almost ensure that he'll finish his career here while also keeping some flexibility, keeping some optionality on it, and we've done that."

For Curry, the choice to return was always a no-brainer, as finishing his career in Golden State has remained a significant factor in his end-of-career decision-making. But Curry reiterated what playing for the Bay Area means to him and the place where he built his legacy.

"This is home; this is what we've built," Curry said at media day. "This is a community that I've played in front of my entire career, and being able to finish the story the right way is a big part of what I can control, thankfully, and hopefully health-wise as well. I know the short list of guys that have been able to do it, but reimagining what that looks like with the level that I feel like I can play at down the stretch of my career and being open to even what this training camp looks like of different ways to approach the game to sustain it as long as I can."

But as for why he landed on the structure of extension, a one-plus-one player option on the back end, the point guard left it up in the air for people to come to their own conclusions.

"I think we're all smart people in this room," Curry said. "You can kind of read the tea leaves on why it's designed the way that it is, for sure."

Typically, players use one-plus-one deals to maintain their own flexibility regarding free agency. Before leaving for the Philadelphia Sixers, LeBron James signed multiple one-plus-one deals with the Los Angeles Lakers, which, in that specific situation, kept pressure on Rob Pelinka and the front office to make moves in accordance with his personal championship window. As for Curry, no reporting or indication points to him doing something similar to the Warriors right now. But the implied threat of declining his player option in 2028 certainly doesn't rule it out.

But for now, and most likely forever, Curry is more than content with staying in Golden State, in the palace that he built.

Steph Curry on why it was important for him to stay with the Warriors.

“There's a pride of representing you know the Bay, representing this franchise that when I stepped foot here in '09 and what we've all been able to accomplish… I want to do right by that.” pic.twitter.com/Y3uaHWTbDJ

— Kenzo Fukuda (@kenzofuku) September 28, 2026

"There's a pride in representing the Bay, representing this franchise that, when I stepped foot here in '09 and what we've all been able to accomplish — this isn't just a me thing, this is a we — I want to do right by that. It's always been an importance for me, and going into this contract decision that was front of mind, for sure."

title: Adam Scott's latest Presidents Cup heartbreak ended with an uncomfortable truth
description: Adam Scott was "desperate" to finally win a Presidents Cup.
fullText:
At the 2024 Open Championship, Adam Scott was asked what kept him and Justin Rose, both of whom came up short of their second major that week, going. Scott delivered his answer with his trademark smile and a chuckle.

"Always being a 'Nearly Great' of the game is spurring us on in our later years," Scott said that Sunday at Troon.

It was honest and illuminating. For all he has achieved in the game — a Masters champion, a Players champion, World No. 1 — Adam Scott still views himself as an underachiever. A year later at the U.S. Open at Oakmont, Scott offered a little more as he entered Sunday with another real chance to finally knock off major No. 2.

"I've put together a nice career, but I think another major would really go a long way in fulfilling my own self, when it's all said and done," Scott said. It was an honest and deeply personal thing for Scott to offer. That for all he has accomplished, he's still searching for the things to fulfill his own self. Things that he knows might never come. And what happens if they don't? What happens if the shadows finally catch him before he can grab one of the things he's still chasing? How do you accept that and find peace?

Adam Scott left Oakmont that week a tough-luck loser as J.J. Spaun roared to victory. Then 44 years old, Scott told The Athletic's Brendan Quinn that he could push on for a little longer, but eventually all things end.

"I feel like I can keep this up for another 18 months, for sure," Scott told Quinn at Oakmont. "Then, at that point, I'll be 46. I think I can push myself for the next year and a half and then reassess, you know?"

Almost 18 months later, Scott is still chasing that final piece — the one that would make him feel his golf journey is complete. While another calendar year went by without major No. 2 arriving, Scott had a chance this past week to achieve another one of his golf heart's great desires, one he has been desperate to check off his list.

Scott made his Presidents Cup debut in 2003, when the Internationals and Americans tied. Since then, Scott has made every Presidents Cup team, and the Internationals have lost every one. Knocking off the Americans and finally hoisting the Presidents Cup has become a version of unfinished business for the International team's elder statesman. He suffered tough losses in 2015 in South Korea and in 2019 in Australia, where the Internationals jumped out to a 9-5 lead before the U.S. rallied for a 16-14 win. On that Sunday in Australia, Scott lost his singles match to Xander Schauffele, a defeat that left a scar.

"I felt like I'd let the side down," Scott told Golfweek's Adam Schupak in 2024. "That one slipped through our fingers. It was months and months and months of trying to figure out how it slipped away because it felt like that was going to be our time. It would have been an epic victory to win there. It's something that I'm still looking for in my career."

All that brings us to last week at Medinah, where Scott and the Internationals arrived in Chicago as heavy underdogs but with the belief that they had the culture and players to knock off the Americans. At the start of the week, Scott was open about his desperation to check this off his list, and the realization that eventually, perhaps someday soon, he won't be on these teams is setting in.

"I want to win one desperately, and I don't know how many more I can possibly play in," Scott said at Medinah.

"I feel like it's a huge opportunity for me," Scott told The Associated Press' Doug Ferguson. "There was probably a period 10 years ago, in the middle of my career, where it was, 'Oh, this (winning) is going to happen.' But now there's not many more, that's for sure. I've been given another chance. It might be the last one."

U.S.'s uneven play at Presidents Cup won't suffice at Ryder Cup

Scott and the Internationals once again jumped out to a lead after sweeping the Friday foursomes session and then held off an American wave on Saturday to take a three-point lead into Sunday. It was the first time in history that the Internationals led entering Sunday on American soil. It seemed like the stars had aligned for Scott to capture one of his remaining white whales and do so in a fashion that would send American golf into a tailspin. But another opportunity to grab self-fulfillment brings the same questions.

How many more chances will there be? If not now, when?

It all seemed set up for the Internationals and Scott to have a storybook Sunday in Chicago. But as has been the story at the Presidents Cup, the Americans blitzed the Internationals in singles, storming back to win 17-13. Scott was among the singles losers. With the Internationals reeling, he needed to flip his match against Patrick Cantlay to give them hope. Instead, Cantlay buried a 57-foot birdie putt on the 16th hole and Scott lost 2 and 1.

With another chance having slipped away, Scott sat at the dais at Medinah and was confronted with what was, what could've been and what lies on the horizon. Scott lauded his teammates but admitted he didn't play well enough against the Americans.

Then, Scott was asked about playing on the team in 2028 or potentially captaining it in Australia.

"I don't know. It's a long way away. Sounds like a lot of work," Scott said on Sunday with a smile and a laugh. "I don't know. It's a long way away. We'll see if I'm — if I can contribute to the team in any way, I'll do whatever for this team."

Scott still has dreams to achieve. He's still ranked 45th in the world, and his ball speed is up. He still has the drive to be one of the best players in the world. He still believes he can add to a resume that feels light, based on his world-class talent and longevity. But he's also a realist. Time keeps moving, and eventually the last of the sand falls through the hourglass.

Eventually, your story is written in the chances that turned to smoke in your hands and in the moments of redemption that never arrived.

The post Adam Scott's latest Presidents Cup heartbreak ended with an uncomfortable truth appeared first on Golf.

title: NFL Giants obtain QB McCarthy from Vikings
description: Second-year NFL quarterback J.J. McCarthy was traded on Monday by Minnesota to the New York Giants, hoping to boost their scoring after a season-ending injury to starting signal-caller Jaxson Dart. The Vikings received a fifth-round pick in next year's NFL Draft for McCarthy, who was selected 10th overall in the 2024 draft but missed the 2024 season with a right knee injury.
fullText:
Second-year NFL quarterback J.J. McCarthy was traded on Monday by Minnesota to the New York Giants, hoping to boost their scoring after a season-ending injury to starting signal-caller Jaxson Dart.

The Vikings received a fifth-round pick in next year's NFL Draft for McCarthy, who was selected 10th overall in the 2024 draft but missed the 2024 season with a right knee injury.

"Really glad, really happy, very excited to add J.J. McCarthy. Think he's a strong young quarterback," said Giants coach John Harbaugh.

"Has some experience in National Football League, obviously was a very high draft pick, very talented player, and is going to make us a stronger football team."

Dart suffered a left knee injury a week ago early in a 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and his replacement, Jameis Winston, struggled in a 12-7 victory over Tennessee last Sunday.

John Harbaugh knows well 23-year-old McCarthy, who played in college at Michigan under Harbaugh's brother Jim, now coach of the Los Angeles Chargers.

"We've been turning over every stone. This was an opportunity that came up. And able to finish the deal off this morning, late morning," said Harbaugh.

However, Harbaugh told reporters that Winston will start the Giants' next game against the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday, and will remain his starting quarterback "as long as I can see into the future."

He indicated that McCarthy will require time to "get to work on learning the offense."

The coach also defended Winston's performance against the Titans on Sunday, noting the quick turnaround from the Giants' previous Monday night game, and the stormy "nor'easter" conditions in which the game in New Jersey was played.

"We'll be ready to play this next game, and going forward, excited about Jameis," he said.

McCarthy went 6-4 last season as a starter for Minnesota, completing 140-of-243 passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns with 12 interceptions. He also ran for 181 yards and four touchdowns.

McCarthy, however, became expendable this season. He lost his starting role this season to free agent signing Kyler Murray, who went into concussion protocol and was replaced by Carson Wentz, who filled in until Murray returned in a 23-16 victory at Tampa Bay for the 3-0 Vikings.

Minnesota saves $4.5 million in salary cap space with the move.

title: ABC’s broadcast audio issues during Texas-Tennessee unrelated to Trump or Secret Service, per report
description: It turns out that the intense static noise during ABC’s broadcast of Texas at Tennessee over the weekend may not have been related to President Donald Trump attending the SEC clash. Before the game, the broadcast’s main storyline focused on how the president and his Secret Service detail could affect communication signals between teams during the game.…
fullText:
It turns out that the intense static noise during ABC's broadcast of Texas at Tennessee over the weekend may not have been related to President Donald Trump attending the SEC clash.

Before the game, the broadcast's main storyline focused on how the president and his Secret Service detail could affect communication signals between teams during the game.

"As you'd expect, Secret Service with heightened security today," said announcer Chris Fowler. "Fans got here very early. Sometimes, when the President moves during a game, it can affect the communication [in] the coaches' headsets and the communication with players on the field."

Reporter Laura Rutledge, however, clarified that both teams cleared their radio signals with the Secret Service and were not expecting any trouble communicating from the upper box to the sideline. The coaches prepared hand signals in case they couldn't call plays to players on the field.

Right after Fowler and Rutledge set the table, game analyst Kirk Herbstreit was almost unintelligible due to the distracting amount of static that cut in when he spoke. Fowler apologized for Herbstreit's sound, and most viewers assumed it was related to the adjustments for Trump. The noise lasted the entire first half.

Right as Laura Rutledge explains Donald Trump’s presence leading to communication issues for Texas and Tennessee, the ABC audio becomes a mess.

Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit try to deliver the play-by-play in a painful listen for ABC viewers. pic.twitter.com/DAESHVhS7u

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 26, 2026

However, according to The Athletic's Andrew Marchand, that was just an unfortunate coincidence.

"You would think, President Trump was there, there was a lot of talk about the Secret Service. It had nothing to do with that, I'm told," Marchand said on his podcast Monday. "Audio board in the truck had problems. That was just coincidental with the president being there, that wasn't the issue."

During last season's College Football Playoff, Indiana faced similar in-helmet communication issues at the Rose Bowl. The technical trouble affected Pat McAfee during his Field Pass alt-cast.

Perhaps the issue is more about the amount of communication equipment and broadcasting capacity involved in big-time football games these days than Trump or the Secret Service.

title: LeBron to New York Was REAL? Lebron Reveals What Changed Everything
description: LeBron James Reveals He Nearly Signed With the Knicks LeBron James is officially a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, but on Monday he revealed that his NBA future nearly took a very different path. During 76ers media day, James told ESPN’s Dave McMenamin that he had envisioned finishing his legendary career with the New York…
fullText:
LeBron James is officially a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, but on Monday he revealed that his NBA future nearly took a very different path.

During 76ers media day, James told ESPN's Dave McMenamin that he had envisioned finishing his legendary career with the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

"I had visions of playing in the Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James said.

James explained that New York was seriously on his mind during free agency. However, the Knicks' championship run ultimately changed everything.

The Knicks won the NBA championship in June, defeating the San Antonio Spurs in the Finals and ending a 53-year championship drought.

After watching New York finally win it all, James decided he could not join the team immediately afterward.

"But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't,'" James said.

James explained that he believed the backlash surrounding him joining the defending champions would have been overwhelming.

"Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all," James said, referring to the media and public reaction.

Instead, James ultimately chose Philadelphia.

James revealed that his final free-agency decision came down to five teams: the 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Knicks were not officially part of that final group, but James acknowledged that New York had been a serious possibility before the championship.

His decision to sign with Philadelphia gave him an opportunity to play alongside Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid while joining a team that believes it can compete for a championship.

James signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the 76ers this offseason.

For Knicks fans, James' comments provide an interesting look at what could have been.

Madison Square Garden has long been one of the most iconic venues in basketball, and James specifically called it the best arena in the world for a basketball player.

Instead of finishing his career in New York, James will begin his 24th NBA season in Philadelphia.

He will still have plenty of opportunities to play at Madison Square Garden, including Philadelphia's regular-season matchup against the Knicks.

The biggest twist is that the Knicks' championship the accomplishment that ended more than five decades of frustration for the franchise may have been the very thing that kept LeBron James from joining them.

For now, Lebron will wear a 76ers jersey.

But Monday's revelation made it clear that a LeBron-Knicks chapter was much closer to happening than many people realized.

title: Blackhawks Finalize Opening-Night Roster, Preview New Forward Lines
description: Before boarding the plane to Las Vegas, the Chicago Blackhawks held one final, intense practice session at the team’s facility […] The post Blackhawks Finalize Opening-Night Roster, Preview New Forward Lines appeared first on Chicago Hockey Now .
fullText:
Before boarding the plane to Las Vegas, the Chicago Blackhawks held one final, intense practice session at the team's facility on Monday morning. It was their last official practice before the 2026-27 regular season begins.

With Landon Slaggert on waivers, the Blackhawks had 23 players attend practice, including defenseman Ethan Del Mastro. Those 23 players will make up the full roster for Tuesday's season-opener against the Vegas Golden Knights.

𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐧𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭 ROLL CALL 🗣️📋

read more 📰 https://t.co/zkZbjlDjOg pic.twitter.com/YBJJWc1f66

— Chicago Blackhawks (@NHLBlackhawks) September 28, 2026

Slaggert and Del Mastro have been battling throughout training camp and the preseason for the 23rd and final NHL roster spot, and it's the scrappy defensive defenseman who came out on top. The Blackhawks will indeed carry 13 forwards, eight defensemen (including both Del Mastro and Kevin Korchinski), and two goaltenders on their opening-night roster.

On Monday afternoon, Slaggert and Dominic Toninato both cleared waivers and will now report to the Rockford IceHogs in the AHL. With Slaggert's penalty-killing skills, hard-nosed style, and strong skating, it was reasonable to think another club would claim him. The Blackhawks can now breathe a sigh of relief that isn't the case.

#Blackhawks forwards Landon Slaggert & Dominic Toninato have cleared waivers & will report to the Rockford IceHogs. https://t.co/t5p1pX8qzc

— Jack Bushman (@JackBushman2) September 28, 2026

Head coach Jeff Blashill spoke about Slaggert's situation following practice, and he made it clear that putting the 23-year-old through waivers wasn't an easy decision for the organization. And with Slaggert officially clearing waivers, Blashill also emphasized that he expects him to make an impact for the NHL club during the elongated 84-game campaign.

"We think we have 14 NHL forwards, so we had hard decisions to make," Blashill said. "That's the decision we made. We feel it's the best decision for us at this time. Those decisions come without a ton of information this year. That's just the way a short camp works. We'll see where it goes… he'll be a guy who helps us at some point this year."

As for the current NHL roster, Blashill made a fascinating decision in the team's final practice before heading out West. He boldly switched up his forward lines, despite little time for the new groups to settle in together.

#Blackhawks lineup ahead of Opening Night:
Moore-Kantserov-Kane
Bertuzzi-Frondell-Mangiapane
Donato-Nazar-Lardis
Smith-Greene-Greenway
Teravainen

Vlasic-Byram
Kaiser-Levshunov
Cole-Rinzel
Korchinski-Del Mastro

Knight
Soderblom

— Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) September 28, 2026

"I just felt ultimately, we just hadn't got enough out of the three lines with the combinations we had used… got to see Roman at center, I feel confident that he can play center in the NHL. [And] I think Frank (Nazar) can carry his own line."

With a stout preseason finale at center, Roman Kantserov remained down the middle during line rushes and drills at practice. Kantserov made his first two preseason appearances on the wing before transitioning to center on Saturday.

Kantserov played center in the Kontinental Hockey League in 2025-26 and thrived, leading the league with 36 goals and becoming the first player under 22 to average a point per game for the entire season. The NHL is a completely different beast, but the Blackhawks must have liked what they saw on Saturday.

Kantserov and Patrick Kane remain together on the top line, but it's no longer Frank Nazar who rounds out the trio, as he did throughout camp and the preseason. Instead, Oliver Moore received a promotion and is in line to play with Kantserov and Kane in Las Vegas.

Blashill believes Moore's pace and 200-foot pressure will help get Kane and Kantserov the puck as much as possible.

"Moore's role on that line is to want to win pucks, make sure he's at the net front, and make the necessary plays. He can't be someone who's turning the puck over… He's got to make sure that there's intent with every play that he makes. It's not trying to make a world-class play every time. I think it suits his game probably better than in some ways in the middle of the ice."

Anton Frondell, Tyler Bertuzzi, and Andrew Mangiapane skated together on Saturday against the St. Louis Blues, and Blashill decided to leave that combination alone. Before the preseason finale, Blashill told the media he wanted a north-south style player to join Frondell and Bertuzzi, as they found success with Ilya Mikheyev on their wing late last year.

Frondell and Bertuzzi both had their best preseason performance in the finale, so the trio remains unchanged for now.

Nazar centered the third line in practice, being joined by Nick Lardis and Ryan Donato. Nazar initially opened training camp as the top-line center with Kantserov and Kane, and the three played well in their first look together last Thursday in St. Louis.

But with Kantserov shining at center on Saturday, Nazar is now further down the lineup, although remaining with an offensive-minded winger in Lardis. Individually, Lardis fared well in the preseason, but didn't mesh with Frondell and Bertuzzi as his linemates. With Nazar's plus skating and heads-up playmaking, the hope is that he'll get Lardis the puck more often, and the two can be dangerous together in transition.

The fourth line of Jordan Greenway, Ryan Greene, and Cole Smith appears to be the only combination that made it through training camp without any changes. However, Blashill emphasized on Monday that he hasn't decided who will be the 13th forward for opening night.

Teuvo Teravainen, who skated as the lone extra forward during practice, is the likely choice to be healthy-scratched in Las Vegas. But Blashill pushed back on that idea when asked about his message to Teravainen heading into the new season.

Jeff Blashill pushes back at the idea that Teuvo Teravainen will definitely be the odd man out for the Blackhawks on Tuesday night… pic.twitter.com/xvKC47IVMp

— CHGO Blackhawks (@CHGO_Blackhawks) September 28, 2026

With a condensed training camp and preseason, Blashill has said multiple times that roster battles will continue throughout October. Specific roles in the lineup could also change from game to game, with still plenty to learn within the NHL group.

title: Star pass rusher Jonathan Greenard set for Eagles' debut against Bears
description: Jonathan Greenard, listed as questionable with a pectoral injury, is expected to make his Eagles debut Monday night against Chicago
fullText:
The Eagles are expected to have Jonathan Greenard available Monday night for the first time.

The pass rusher is set to make his Philadelphia debut against the Chicago Bears, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported. Greenard was listed as questionable with a pectoral injury after practicing in full ahead of the game. His status will become official when the Eagles release their inactive list. Philadelphia acquired Greenard from Minnesota during draft weekend, but the injury kept him out of training camp and the first two regular-season games. He returned to practice before the opener and gradually increased his work. Getting through a full practice this week was his clearest step toward playing.

Greenard's return would give defensive coordinator Vic Fangio another established edge rusher as the Eagles try to move to 3-0. Philadelphia has managed his recovery carefully, and his first-game snap total remains to be seen. A limited workload would still let the Eagles work him into their pass-rush rotation.

Pass rusher Jonathan Greenard (questionable, pec) is set to make his Philadelphia Eagles debut tonight vs. Chicago, per source. pic.twitter.com/cwqZsHNWml

The timing also matters for a defense facing Chicago on the road in prime time. The Eagles have played their first two games without one of their major offseason additions. Monday offers their first chance to see what Greenard can add.

title: Joel Klatt has a new No. 1 in Top 10 rankings after Week 4
description: Joel Klatt released his top 10 rankings after an exciting Week 4, and he moved the Georgia Bulldogs up
fullText:
Joel Klatt released his top 10 rankings after Week 4 of the college football season, and the Georgia Bulldogs were the beneficiaries of the ultimate promotion. They rose up to the No. 1 spot in his rankings.

They earned the No. 1 spot after their dominating 41-13 win over Oklahoma. "There's something about that team, that head coach. We haven't had to see Gunner Stockton be great in the fourth quarter, but we know he can be. So I'm not even worried that they're not in a one-possession game," said Klatt.

He doesn't think Georgia is perfect, though.

"Do I still have concerns about some areas of their team? Yes, just like everybody has some flaws. I don't know how they can throw the football, and Stockton threw a pick in that game. Georgia jumped out to a 28-0 halftime lead. It was 41-13 in that game, but they only had 306 yards of total offense," said Klatt. Kirby Smart and Gunner Stockton deserve a lot of trust, but there's definitely a higher bar for the offense to clear.

Klatt brought Georgia up to No. 1 partially because he was unimpressed with what the former No. 1 Texas Longhorns delivered against Tennessee. Texas won 20-17, but the game wasn't pretty, and the Longhorns nearly lost. "I had Texas at No. 1. I was honoring that win against Ohio State, but Texas is going to drop a spot because, let's face it, that was incredibly sloppy," said Klatt.

There are a lot of new teams in his rankings. Florida and Oregon slide up into the top 10 at No. 8 and 9, respectively. LSU and Ole Miss dropped out of his top 10 from last week. "That was a resounding win, albeit at home, but a resounding win. They beat Ole Miss, and they did it with 53 rushes for 300 yards," Klatt said on Florida.

Oregon won against USC 41-27 on the road. "I don't know if I would want to play Oregon, and I certainly wouldn't want to play them in their own building," said Klatt.

With Ole Miss's and LSU's departure from the top 10, the Miami Hurricanes (No. 4) rise one spot, Notre Dame (No. 5) rises two spots, and Alabama (No. 6) rises three spots. The Indiana Hoosiers (No. 7) go down one spot after barely squeaking by Northwestern.

title: Astros weren't great in regular season, but neither were these teams that reached World Series
description: The Astros are the first team with a .500 record to make the MLB postseason. They can look this list of teams who also underachieved in the regular season, but got hot at the right time.
fullText:
You know what they call a team with a mediocre regular season record that gets hot at the right time and wins the World Series? Champions.

That's all the Houston Astros care about as they enter the postseason with the distinction of being the sport's playoff-qualifier with the fewest wins in a complete 162-game schedule.

Still, they're in the postseason, which means, beginning with Tuesday's start of the wild-card series against the Chicago White Sox, they're 14 victories away from winning a World Series that brings with it a banner that will fly just as high and a trophy that will shine just as bright as the other two in franchise history.

If the Astros need any encouragement, they can look at history and find plenty of teams who had discouraging regular seasons, but found their stride in October and went all the way to the World Series.

Here are the teams with the worst regular seasons that still made it to the end…

Lost World Series
Before the current version of the Astros came along, the Mets and the 2005 San Diego Padres owned the record for playoff teams with the fewest wins in a full regular season. Unlike the Padres, the Mets, led by 1973 Cy Young Award winner Tom Seaver and managed by Yogi Berra, made it all the way to the World Series. The Mets, who became known for Tug McGraw's catchphrase "Ya Gotta Believe!!!", were in last place with a month to play and five games below .500 on Sept. 11 before winning 12 of their final 16 games. They beat the vaunted Big Red Machine of the Cincinnati Reds in the NLCS and had a 3-2 series lead on the Oakland Athletics before dropping Games 6 and 7 to lose the World Series.

Won World Series
The Cardinals, whose .516 winning percentage is the lowest for any World Series champion, had two separate eight-game losing streaks - by comparison, the Astros lost eight in a row once in April - and a seven-game losing streak, but still outpaced the Astros by 1 ½ games in a weak National League Central. They went on to shock the San Diego Padres in the NLDS and take out the New York Mets in a seven-game NLCS before coasting past Justin Verlander and the Detroit Tigers in just five games in the World Series. The light-hitting David Eckstein was named World Series MVP for hitting .364 against the Tigers.

Lost World Series
The Diamondbacks narrowly earned a wild-card spot despite getting swept by the Astros in the regular season's final series, which the Astros needed to edge out the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Arizona upset the Brewers in the wild-card series, then swept the Dodgers in the NLDS despite finishing 16 games behind them in the NL West. The Diamondbacks, who were led offensively by current Astros first baseman Christian Walker, needed seven games to beat the Phillies in the NLCS before finally succumbing to the Rangers, who had eliminated the Astros in a tense seven-game ALCS.

Won World Series
Before the 2006 St. Louis Cardinals came along, this Twins team was the worst to win a World Series. The Kirby Puckett-led Twins went just 29-52 on the road in the regular season but used the raucous Metrodome to their advantage in the postseason, winning all four home games over the St. Louis Cardinals in the World Series. The Twins still are the only team with a losing run differential in the regular season to go on and win the World Series. The Twins were outscored by 20 runs in the regular season, while the current Astros were outscored by 32.

Won World Series
It's tough to think about any of those Yankees teams that three-peated from 1998-2000 as not great, but the last team of that title run limped to the finish, losing 15 of its final 18 games while still managing to hold off the Boston Red Sox for a playoff spot. Once the Yankees were in, though, they got hot and beat the Athletics in a thrilling five-game ALDS before finishing off the Mariners in six games in the ALCS. With Andy Pettitte and Roger Clemens leading the pitching staff, the Yankees crushed the Mets in a Subway World Series that included Clemens chunking a broken bat at Mets slugger Mike Piazza during Game 2.

Lost World Series
Cleveland was the beneficiary of playing in a weak American League Central where no other team finished above .500 that season. Still, Cleveland had a potent offense with Jim Thome, Matt Williams and David Justice each hitting more than 30 home runs. Cleveland went through the Yankees and Orioles in the playoffs before falling to the Florida Marlins in a thrilling seven-game World Series that ended with a walk-off single from Édgar Rentería.

Lost World Series
Astros fans all know what ultimately happened to this Phillies team, but it was a feat that it even made it this far. Philadelphia got off to such a poor start that manager Joe Girardi was fired in June. Under interim manager Rob Thomson, the Phillies went 65-46 the rest of the way to make the playoffs by one game. From there, they eliminated the Cardinals, Braves and Padres before running into the Astros, who had won 106 regular-season games and finished off Philadelphia in six games.

Won World Series
The 2014 World Series pitted two teams that didn't reach 90 wins in the regular season with the 89-73 Kansas City Royals falling to the 88-74 Giants. That Giants team didn't have much of an offense with no one one the team reaching 25 home runs or 90 RBIs, but it rode the arm of Madison Bumgarner in the postseason. Bumgarner, who threw a complete-game shutout in Game 5 of the World Series and came back to throw five scoreless innings of relief in Game 7, pitched a remarkable seven times in that playoff run, putting up a 1.03 ERA in 52 ⅔ innings.

Won World Series
Astros fans are plenty familiar with this team. The Braves entered the postseason with the worst record of anyone in the playoffs that year. They were 5 games out in August, but went 36-18 over the final two months of the regular season and kept that hot streak going in the postseason, including beating the 95-win Astros in six games in the World Series. Jorge Soler, who hit a ball completely out of the Astros' home ballpark, was named World Series MVP.

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle.

title: Former NFL Player Calls Out ‘Idiotic Coaching’ That Resulted in Baker Mayfield’s Injury
description: Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho criticized the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ decision-making after Baker Mayfield suffered an injury during a costly sequence against the Minnesota Vikings. Acho questioned the choice to attempt a fourth-and-13 from Tampa Bay’s own 39-yard line, a decision that ended with an interception and Mayfield getting hurt on the play. fullText:
Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho criticized the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' decision-making after Baker Mayfield suffered an injury during a costly sequence against the Minnesota Vikings. Acho questioned the choice to attempt a fourth-and-13 from Tampa Bay's own 39-yard line, a decision that ended with an interception and Mayfield getting hurt on the play.

The Buccaneers entered the situation trailing by four points but still had all three timeouts available. Instead of punting and forcing Minnesota's struggling offense to drive the length of the field, Tampa Bay elected to keep its offense on the field for a difficult fourth-down conversion attempt.

The decision carried significant risk given the field position and distance needed for a first down. Mayfield dropped back and attempted to make a play, but the possession ended with an interception, turning an aggressive decision into a major setback for a team already searching for answers.

The consequences became even more concerning when Mayfield was injured during the sequence. The quarterback suffered a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, adding another layer of uncertainty to a Buccaneers team that had already endured a difficult start to the season.

Acho shared his thoughts about how Tampa Bays' coaching led to Mayfield's injury. This can be seen in a post he made on his official X account.

There’s some really idiotic coaching in the NFL—

The Buccaneers have 3 timeouts and are at their own 39, down by 4. They decide to go for it on 4th and 13 as opposed to punting it to a struggling Kyler Murray.

The play results in Mayfield hurt after throwing an interception.

— Emmanuel Acho (@EmmanuelAcho) September 27, 2026

Acho's reaction focused on the coaching decision rather than simply the turnover or injury itself. His criticism centered on the opportunity Tampa Bay had to punt, rely on its defense and put pressure on Minnesota's offense, particularly with the Vikings' quarterback struggling to generate consistent production.

The sequence ultimately became a defining moment in another frustrating afternoon for Tampa Bay. The fourth-down gamble failed to produce the needed conversion, Mayfield left the play injured and the Buccaneers were left to deal with both the immediate consequences and questions about the decision that created such a high-risk situation.

title: Raul Rosas Jr. thought Raoni Barcelos died during UFC Vegas 121 headliner
description: Raul Rosas Jr. thought Raoni Barcelos died during their five-round war at UFC Vegas 121.
fullText:
Raul Rosas Jr. feared the worst at UFC Vegas 121.

The young star collided with the tried-and-tested Raoni Barcelos in the headlining bout of Saturday's event. After a war that went deep into the final round, Rosas Jr. came out on top, under bizarre circumstances. Barcelos seemingly lost consciousness through minimal contact, falling to the canvas, and being stretchered out of the octagon with doctors checking his pulse. Many believe the pace of the fight was too much for the aging bantamweight, but Rosas Jr. is just glad that his opponent is in good health.

Positive updates have surfaced in the days following UFC Vegas 121. Barcelos is reportedly in good spirits, and while pleased with the news, Rosas Jr. initially believed the Brazilian was dead.

"I'm happy to know that Raoni Barcelos is back up and is breathing, because at the end of the day, we've all got a family to go back to," Rosas Jr. said. "I don't know if he has kids or not, but either way, he has a lot of people that love him. He's a really great person. So, I'm happy about that."

"For a second, I didn't know if he died, to be honest. But then, when I calmed myself down a little bit and I was looking, I checked if he was breathing, and I saw his body breathing. So I was like, he's not dead for sure. That made me feel a little bit more peaceful. I was just sitting there praying; I just did a quick prayer and hoped that he woke up and went back to his family."

With the scary prospect of a UFC death behind him, Raul Rosas Jr. revealed that he was happy with his own performance. A tough win against a crafty veteran, the fight gave Rosas Jr. confidence about his chances against other elite opponents.

"It was scary because of that, but to be honest, yes, I was happy about my performance on the side… I was happy to take the fight because I was like, man, if I can't beat him, then I can't be champion. I need a challenge like this. This is exactly what I needed to prove to myself that I belong here."

title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford Makes Unwanted History in Shocking Loss to Broncos
description: Matthew Stafford made NFL history for an unwanted reason as the Los Angeles Rams suffered a stunning 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos. The veteran quarterback threw his 33rd career pick-six, surpassing Brett Favre for the most in league history. The record-breaking play came with the Rams holding a 19-16 lead in the fourth quarter. […] The post Rams QB Matthew Stafford Makes Unwanted History in Shocking Loss to Broncos appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Matthew Stafford made NFL history for an unwanted reason as the Los Angeles Rams suffered a stunning 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos. The veteran quarterback threw his 33rd career pick-six, surpassing Brett Favre for the most in league history.

The record-breaking play came with the Rams holding a 19-16 lead in the fourth quarter. Talanoa Hufanga jumped in front of a pass intended for Kyren Williams and returned the interception 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead of the night.

The mistake was particularly costly because Los Angeles had controlled much of the game early. The Rams carried a 16-0 advantage into halftime before the Broncos mounted a second-half comeback, turning the contest into a back-and-forth battle that remained undecided until the final seconds.

Stafford did not allow the interception to derail him immediately, responding with a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield on the next possession. That score put Los Angeles back in front 26-23, demonstrating how quickly the veteran quarterback could recover from a major mistake and keep his team within striking distance.

Stafford recently made unwanted history as his team lost to the Broncos this week. This can be seen in a post shared by NFL Researcher on X.

Most pick sixes thrown in NFL history…

1. Matthew Stafford – 33
2. Brett Favre – 32
3. Dan Marino – 29
4. Joe Namath – 28
5. Peyton Manning – 27
5. Drew Brees – 27

— NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) September 28, 2026

However, Denver answered with a late touchdown, and the Rams received one final opportunity to steal the game. Stafford drove Los Angeles inside the Denver 20-yard line, but Hufanga intercepted another pass in the end zone as time expired, finishing a night in which the safety recorded both of the quarterback's interceptions.

Stafford finished with 390 passing yards and two touchdowns, but the two interceptions proved decisive in the four-point defeat. The record now belongs to him, but the more immediate concern for Los Angeles is recovering from a game it once appeared poised to win and correcting the mistakes that turned a 16-point lead into a damaging loss.

fullText:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith put on a spectacular performance against Illinois on Saturday, racking up 12 catches for 217 yards and four — yes, four — touchdowns in a 42-19 win for No. 5 Ohio State. Oddsmakers have installed Smith (+275 at BetMGM) as the new betting favorite to win the Heisman Trophy as a result.

Smith entered the weekend's games with 10-1 odds, but jumped several players, including Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss — who were the co-favorites to win the Heisman at BetMGM entering Week 4.

Smith currently has the most wagers (9.2%) and most money wagered (18.2%) of any player to win the Heisman at BetMGM, and represents the sportsbook's biggest liability. Only one wide receiver (Alabama's Devonta Smith in 2020) has won the Heisman since 1992.

Mensah (+400) has the second-best odds and has been impressive early on, throwing eight touchdowns and leading No. 4-ranked Miami to a 4-0 record.

Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor opened with 150-1 odds to win the Heisman and has shot up all the way to +700 (third-best odds) after a strong start to the season. Taylor is tied for the lead in college football with 14 TD passes, and Mississippi State owns a 4-0 record, heading into a showdown with No. 7 Alabama on Saturday.

Notre Dame QB CJ Carr — the preseason Heisman favorite — has 12-1 odds, while Texas QB Arch Manning has dropped all the way to 30-1 .

title: Braves put trust in Sale to anchor depleted rotation in NL Wild Card Series against Phillies
description: The Atlanta Braves battled through a long list of pitching injuries that left their rotation depleted for their National League Wild Card Series against the Philadelphia Phillies.  “For sure, it’s a different feeling when a guy like that is taking the mound on a big day,” Weiss said Monday.  The NL East champion Braves (94-68) went 9-4 against the second-place Phillies (88-74) and finished six games ahead of them in the regular season.
fullText:
ATLANTA (AP) — The Atlanta Braves battled through a long list of pitching injuries that left their rotation depleted for their National League Wild Card Series against the Philadelphia Phillies.

That's why manager Walt Weiss and Braves players are glad to have ace left-hander Chris Sale on the mound for Tuesday's opening game in the best-of-three series.

"For sure, it's a different feeling when a guy like that is taking the mound on a big day," Weiss said Monday.

Added first baseman Matt Olson: "It's a great feeling. He's been nothing short of amazing for us ... just the teammate and the pitcher and the bulldog he is on the mound. I wouldn't want anyone else starting for us."

The NL East champion Braves (94-68) went 9-4 against the second-place Phillies (88-74) and finished six games ahead of them in the regular season. Sale (14-9, 2.16 ERA) was 4-0 versus Philadelphia with a 2.08 ERA.

"He's got to be one of the top two lefties in the league, top few pitchers in the league, so yeah, he presents a whole set of problems. But we've seen him a little bit," said Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly. "You know, we haven't been great against him, but we'll see. Tomorrow's a new day."

Phillies All-Star left-hander Jesús Luzardo (14-5, 2.86) will start as an opener after being used for a scoreless eighth inning in Sunday's 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays that finally clinched the third NL wild-card spot.

Luzardo returned from a stint on the injured list with left shoulder inflammation. The wild-card opener will be his first start since throwing his first career shutout in a 1-0 home win over Atlanta on Sept. 7.

Right-hander Tyler Mahle likely will be Atlanta's Game 2 starter. Left-hander Martín Pérez could have been the third starter before landing on the 15-day injured list Thursday with lower back inflammation. The Braves also have lost starting pitchers Spencer Schwellenbach, Spencer Strider, Reynaldo López and Hurston Waldrep this season.

Luzardo might remain in the game longer than a normal opener if he comes close to the form he showed in recording 12 strikeouts in the shutout win over the Braves.

Mattingly said Monday he was glad Luzardo logged the inning on Sunday so he could "see the bounce-back today."

When asked if it was necessary to use Luzardo in the relief role if starting the Wild Card Series opener was an option, Mattingly said he wasn't taking any chances in Sunday's must-win situation.

"I don't think it was a 100% had to," Mattingly said. "But, you know, in that game, you're not gonna let anything get away, right? You're not going to let this thing creep back into a game, that type of thing."

Luzardo was the NL pitcher of the month in August. He was efficient in the shutout win over the Braves, allowing only two hits and one walk. The game lasted just 1 hour, 51 minutes.

Mattingly said second baseman Luis Arraez will not be on the Wild Card Series roster after spraining his left ankle on Thursday. Right-hander Jonathan Bowlan (groin) will be available.

Braves right-hander Bryce Elder, expected to miss three to four weeks after surgery on his right knee Sept. 8, threw batting practice Monday but will not be on the roster for the series. Right-hander Joe Jiménez, who hasn't pitched since 2024 due to three operations on his left knee, also threw batting practice. Weiss indicated Elder might have a chance to return if the Braves advance to the Division Series.

Following a celebration in the clubhouse after Sunday's win, the Phillies had a quick flight to Atlanta for Monday's workout. Mattingly and his players were still reflecting on the stressful final week of the regular season that included four straight losses before the clinching win.

"It kind of feels like it sums up our whole season a little bit," shortstop Trea Turner said. "Playing well at times, playing bad at times, getting unlucky sometimes. Just felt a little frustrating as a group. I think we knew that. We wanted to play well. We wanted to get in as soon as possible. You don't want to wait until the last day."

fullText:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Donovan Mitchell and his Cleveland Cavaliers teammates didn't go their separate ways for four months before reassembling a couple weeks ago for the start of offseason workouts.

Instead, from the time the Cavaliers were eliminated in the Eastern Conference finals by the New York Knicks until Monday's media day, which marked the unofficial start of training camp, the group has spent a lot of time around each other.

"I think this is probably the most time I've spent with my teammates outside of the actual season in my career," Mitchell said. "From being in New York at the (US) Open and working out there and then going to James' (Harden's) birthday and working out there. And the crazy part is none of us went to summer league (in Las Vegas)."

James Harden was at the forefront of building the team bonding during the offseason. Harden was a midseason acquisition last year, but really didn't get to know his teammates off the court until the summer.

"We really didn't have an opportunity to have that team bond, games in the regular season. And then you're preparing for the postseason everything is intensified. So this summer was a really good opportunity for us to learn each other," he said. "Understanding somebody that's like any job in the world. Now it's giving them comfortability to come talk to me or me talk to them in ways that we never really had before. I think we've built some really good stuff over these last few months."

Besides the time spent around teammates, both showed their commitment by signing new contracts during the offseason.

Mitchell inked a four-year, $273-million contract extension on the first day of the offseason signing period. The seven-time All-Star had two seasons remaining on his contract and could have waited to re-sign until next summer, when he would be eligible for a five-year supermax deal worth $350 million.

"I could have waited and made it about myself and whatnot, but for me, how can we as a team go out there and find a way to make moves? I've said to him (vice president of basketball operations Koby Altman) I want to be here. I've said it publicly and I love being here. And I think for me, now it's about delivering and everything else that comes with it," Mitchell said.

Harden signed a three-year, $97 million contract last month after declining his player option. He also helped recruit acquiring Peyton Watson in a five-team trade.

"I think it was a no-brainer. He's young, he's athletic, he's gotten a lot better and it just fits what we're trying to do. He's been in postseason runs with Denver, so he knows what that looks like," Harden said of Watson.

Center Thomas Bryant, who also re-signed with the Cavaliers during the offseason, said the biggest group during the offseason is that everyone is speaking the same language when it comes to running plays. That's something that didn't happen last season with the midseason trades and also the Cavaliers having 41 different starting lineups during the regular season due to injuries.

"We're having these now before we even started the new year with the team. I think that's a great step of growth going forward," he said.

Mitchell and Harden will need to put together big seasons again if the Cavaliers are going to contend in the Eastern Conference. The 29-year old Mitchell averaged 27.9 points, 5.7 assists and 4.5 rebounds during the regular season, along with 26 points in the playoffs.

The 36-year-old Harden is going into his 18th NBA season. He averaged 10.7 points for the Cavaliers in the regular season, and 19.7 points in the postseason.

The team bonding will continue over the next week as the Cavaliers hold training camp in Spain. They open the regular season on Oct. 22 at Philadelphia against LeBron James and the 76ers.

"More time together equals more success, in my mind. Number one, it's just a good group of guys we've got here. If you're willing to sacrifice for each other, that goes such a long way that nothing can make up for," center Jarrett Allen said.

title: Attention Michigan Fans: Mark Dantonio is on the CFP Selection Committee
description: It’s been a nightmare start to Michigan’s football season, but could the worst be yet to come? Printed on t-shirts, […]
fullText:
It's been a nightmare start to Michigan's football season, but could the worst be yet to come?

Printed on t-shirts, sweatshirts and bumper stickers for the past four years, the message has been clear: "Michigan vs Everybody."

And after Wolverines' last-second win over Western Michigan in the season opener, it seemed like "Everybody" was dumping on college football's winningest program.

Now Michigan is coming off its first official loss of the season after Iowa's last-second touchdown pass in the Big House Saturday left the Wolverine nation stunned, reeling and looking under the bed for anybody.

The result, Michigan fell completely out of the Associated Press Top 25 poll and clung to No. 24 in the AFCA Coaches Poll this week.

With the loss, many people insist on viewing Michigan as 2-2 team rather than its actual 3-1 record. The Wolverines have eight games remaining on their regular-season schedule and they may have to win them all — and the Big Ten title — to reach the College Football Playoffs.

If Michigan slips again, and finishes 10-2 without reaching the conference title game, a plethora of onlookers will view the Maize and Blue as 9-3 and not worthy of a postseason berth.

Three-loss teams were viewed as longshots or having no chance of making the College Football Playoffs under the 12-team format until Alabama seized an at-large berth this past season.

Three-loss Clemson reached the CFP in 2024, but all the Tigers' losses came in the regular season, and they won an automatic berth after winning the ACC conference title.

If Michigan gets hot and finishes 10-2, or 9-3, without winning the conference title or reaching the title game, its fate falls squarely into the hands of the CFP Selection Committee members.

This year, a batch of new faces joined the Committee, including former Michigan State head coach Mark Dantonio, who is not exactly known for being Michigan's biggest fan.

Dantonio, a College Football Hall of Fame member, was born in Ohio and was a defensive coordinator at Ohio State, serving two stints, one for Earl Bruce and the second under Jim Tressel.

CFP committee members are chosen based on their knowledge of the game, objectivity, principles and ethics.

Over the course of 13 seasons at MSU, a long Dantonio-Michigan feud reached a boiling point on several occasions, which may now leave many Michigan fans wondering if the Wolverines would get a fair shake in the committee room come December.

The feud began to grab national attention in 2007 when Michigan topped MSU 28-24 and Michigan running back Mike Hart referred to the Spartans as "little brother" during his postgame interview.

"Sometimes you get your little brother excited when you're playing basketball and stuff, let them get the lead, and then you just come back and take it back," Hart said.

Also serving on the CFP Selection Committee are: Arkansas AD and Chairperson Hunter Yurachek, Athletic Directors Troy Dannen (Nebraska), Mark Harlan (Utah), Chris Massaro (Middle Tennessee), Doug Gillin (Appalachian State) and Carla Wiliams (Virginia), retired media analyst Ivan Maisel, former Auburn and UCF coach Gus Matzahn, former Nebraska and Oregon State coach Mike Riley, former Fresno State and California coach Jeff Tedford and former All-Americans Randall McDaniel and Wesley Walls.

title: Brandel Chamblee tells Phil Mickelson what he must do now to be welcomed back by most golf fans
description: Brandel Chamblee believes that there is still an opportunity for Phil Mickelson to be welcomed back into the fold by the majority of golf fans should he apologise for his role in LIV Golf’s rise. Mickelson has not been seen at a LIV Golf event since March, with his appearance in South Africa proving to be his only start of the season.
fullText:
Brandel Chamblee believes that there is still an opportunity for Phil Mickelson to be welcomed back into the fold by the majority of golf fans should he apologise for his role in LIV Golf's rise.

Mickelson has not been seen at a LIV Golf event since March, with his appearance in South Africa proving to be his only start of the season. He had been dealing with a private matter in the early part of the year.

You would have to go back to 1989 for the last time Mickelson went an entire season without playing in one of the majors. That was the year that Rory McIlroy was born.

From the outside, it appears that there are now serious question marks over whether Mickelson will play in another tournament.

The uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf's future adds another layer to the story. Mickelson's decision to hold talks with the league in the months after he made history at the 2021 PGA Championship severely damaged his reputation.

And as there is no question that many players would have been inspired to join LIV because of Mickelson's interest, it is difficult to see any way back for him as a figure associated with the PGA Tour.

Speaking on the We Need a Fourth podcast, Brandel Chamblee was asked whether he has tarnished his legacy for good. Interestingly, Chamblee claimed that there is still an opportunity for the 56-year-old.

"I don't know about forever. I think we're in a pretty forgiving world. He's obviously got his demons that he fights, and I wouldn't wish them on anybody, but he's not alone in fighting demons. I think if he hadn't gone to LIV, he would have been Arnold Palmer reincarnated. He would have been Ryder Cup captain numerous times. He would have been an honorary starter at Augusta. He would have been the lead analyst at CBS. He would have been the pied piper everywhere he went," he said.

"But I think if he came back and said 'look, I've made mistakes, I've tried to deal with them. Sorry for the damage I've caused. The game's been so good to me. And for the rest of my life, I'm going to try and be good back to it', I think everyone would put their arms around him and go 'welcome back, sorry you had so much trouble, hope you get your life straightened out'. Life's hard, it doesn't matter who you're talking into, running into. Everybody's dealing with something. Everybody's got some battle that they've faced or will face.

"I started doing commentary in 2004, so 2004 until Phil left, I used to say Phil was a gift to the game of golf. His talent, his showmanship, his look at me quality, it was incredible. What a talent, what an amazing talent."

Few would have ever thought when Mickelson was making his way down the 72nd hole at Kiawah Island that he would be in his current position five years later.

As Chamblee suggests, it looked nailed on that he would lead the American Ryder Cup team at Bethpage Black, while he would have almost certainly been a Presidents Cup captain, too.

Many would have expected Mickelson and Tiger Woods to renew their rivalry on PGA Tour Champions. Instead, there is good reason to think that neither should play in a competitive event again.

Perhaps the pair will surprise us again in the future. However, there may be plenty of fans who feel that too much damage has been done and it is time to move on from two legendary figures who have undoubtedly changed the game.

title: Drake Maye's struggles hovering over Patriots' slow start with division opener next
description: Drake Maye wasn’t one of the things the Patriots anticipated having to worry about entering this season.  After beginning the season with two games of uneven play, Maye’s struggles found a new floor in the Patriots’ 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.  “I’ve got to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point,” Maye said.
fullText:
Drake Maye wasn't one of the things the Patriots anticipated having to worry about entering this season.

Suddenly, the third-year quarterback is at the top of the list.

After beginning the season with two games of uneven play, Maye's struggles found a new floor in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

He went without a touchdown pass for the second straight game, while completing a season-low 56% (14 of 25) of his throws, tossing two interceptions and losing one of his two fumbles on the day.

"I've got to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point," Maye said. "It's Week 3, and at the same time we've got to get some fuel and realize that what we're doing out there offensively is unacceptable. It's been unacceptable for three weeks. So, I've got to start with myself and then lead these guys, and we've got to get back after it."

Maye's six interceptions are the most by a Patriots quarterback through three games since Drew Bledsoe (eight) in his second NFL season in 1994. Maye had only eight in all of the 2025 season.

What's worse, Maye seems unsure of himself when he drops back to pass. He has tried to force the ball to well-covered wide receivers at times, while badly overthrowing receivers in other instances. Turning the page on those miscues also has been a problem, he acknowledged.

"I think it's beating myself and realizing that there's times last year where you gotta flip to the next play and realize that this league will humble you quick and just finding ways for me to step up when I feel like I'm not playing my best and still lead the team," Maye said. "I think that's what this position is about."

One of the things that got a lot of attention Sunday was a moment in the third quarter between Maye and coach Mike Vrabel on the sideline. Vrabel stood in front of his visibly downtrodden quarterback and placed both hands on his shoulders while speaking to him for an extended period.

Vrabel believes part of helping get Maye out of this funk is reminding him that Maye still has room to grow.

"I try to talk to him about, just taking the ball and putting it where it's supposed to go. And he's 24 years old. Like we're not dealing with a 35-year-old quarterback here," Vrabel said. "He's a young quarterback. I want him to go and be energetic and talk to him about, just, can't be a robot here. We've got to go. And you saw sometimes where he extended plays and kept his eyes downfield and made plays, and then also we just can't turn it over the rate that we're turning it over, especially down in the red zone."

Despite their inability to put the ball in the end zone, the Patriots' ability to move the ball beyond the 50-yard line on seven drives shows that the offense can sustain drives.

Moving the ball is one thing, but the results of those possessions showed just how dismal a day it was. In order, New England's drives that advanced to Jacksonville territory resulted in a punt, fumble, field goal, interception, missed field goal, field goal and turnover on downs. That feeds into what the overall story is on offense.

The Patriots have scored only 29 points in 30 drives this season. That's the fewest points per drive (0.97) by any team through three games since the 2021 New York Jets.

Cornerback Marcus Jones provided one of the few bright spots on defense, picking off Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. It was Jones' seventh career interception.

Mack Hollins. With the Patriots trailing 28-3 in the fourth quarter and facing third-and-10 on the Jacksonville 16, Maye completed a 9-yard pass to Hollins for what would have been a first down at the 7. Instead, Hollins' celebration after the catch drew a 15-yard taunting penalty.

It forced the Patriots to settle for Andy Borregales' 40-yard field goal.

Right guard Greg Van Roten left in the first half with a thigh injury and did not return. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore (shoulder) and cornerback Carlton Davis III also missed snaps but returned.

19 — The number of fumbles (nine) and interceptions (10) Maye has had since the start of last season's playoffs — a total of seven games. He's the first player with nine or more fumbles and 10 or more interceptions in a seven-game span since Jameis Winston did it in 2019 during his 30- touchdown, 30-interception season.

The Patriots stay on the road, travelling to Buffalo for their AFC East opener on Sunday.

title: Texas softball starts fall ball Tuesday. How to watch Teagan Kavan, Katie Stewart
description: Teagan Kavan, Katie Stewart and new faces like Isa Torres start fall ball for Texas softball
fullText:
Sure, Texas softball doesn't officially start defense of its national championship until early February. But like most teams across the country, the Longhorns play an abbreviated schedule in the fall that helps solidify the pitching rotation, determine the lineup and lay the foundation for what head coach Mike White and his program hope is a third consecutive championship run.

Texas begins fall ball Tuesday against Murray State. Here are five things to know about the Longhorns' fall schedule:

After Texas kicks off its fall schedule by hosting Murray State Tuesday (6 p.m. at McCombs Field), the Longhorns will host four more games: Oct. 13 against Texas State, Oct. 20 against Temple College, Oct. 27 against McLennan Community College and Oct. 29 against UTSA.

Texas will visit Texas A&M for its final fall game Nov. 6 at 7 p.m. at Davis Diamond in College Station.

MORE: PHOTOS: Best images from Texas softball's Women's College World Series championship wins

Tickets to McCombs Field during the regular season often sell out, and all of the seats in the infield bleachers are not available expect through season tickets. But all fall ball home games at McCombs Field are free to the public, with seats in the infield and outfield available on a first-come, first-serve basis.

Outfielder Zoey Abdullah becomes third Texas Longhorns softball pledge for 2028

Texas must replace a handful of players from the 2026 team that went 53-12 and beat Texas Tech for the second consecutive season in the Women's College World Series finals. They include four-year starting right-fielder Ashton Maloney, record-setting catcher Reese Atwood, All-American second baseman Leighann Goode and versatile pitcher Citlaly Gutierrez.

Pitcher Teagan Kavan returns for her fourth season as arguably the greatest clutch pitcher in the college game. She became the first player to win consecutive WCWS Most Outstanding Player awards this past season after earning four complete-game wins in Oklahoma City as well as the save in the title-clinching 4-1 win over the Red Raiders.

Texas also welcomes back All-Americans in first baseman Katie Stewart and outfielder Kayden Henry as well as star infielder Vivi Martinez and sophomore pitcher/slugger Hannah Wells.

Texas will replace the holes in its roster with a seven-player high school recruiting class that ranks third in the nation by On3 and a three-player transfer class listed as No. 2 by D1 Softball.

Infielder Isa Torres and catcher Samantha Swan, former teammates at Georgetown High School, transferred in from Florida State and Arizona State, respectively. Both earned All-American honors last season, and both are expected to slide into starting roles for Texas.

Among the freshmen, infielder Annie Abdullah, infielder Mia Clemmer and pitcher Madi Doty all rank as consensus top 20 national recruits and look poised for an early impact.

title: Pochettino: Manchester City verdicts show fans ‘lived through an era of deception’
description: US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino expressed dismay at news of Manchester City being found guilty of widespread financial improprieties on Monday, saying that fans “lived through a period of deception” because of City’s alleged financial impropriety.  The Guardian and other outlets have reported that Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of violating the vast majority of 115 different charges concerning violations of financial rules between 2009 and 2018.  Pochettino was the manager of Tottenham Hotspur for five seasons, from 2014 to 2019, and of Southampton before that from 2013 to 2014.
fullText:
US men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino expressed dismay at news of Manchester City being found guilty of widespread financial improprieties on Monday, saying that fans "lived through a period of deception" because of City's rule breaches.

The Guardian and other outlets have reported that Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of violating the vast majority of 115 different charges concerning violations of financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

Pochettino was the manager of Tottenham Hotspur for five seasons, from 2014 to 2019, and of Southampton before that from 2013 to 2014. He also took charge of Chelsea for a single season in 2023-24.

"Where were the controls?" Pochettino said in Spanish, when asked by the Guardian for his thoughts on the guilty verdicts. "That's what gets my attention. Where were the controls?

"If I remember being at Southampton, then Tottenham – I remember building [the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] and not having the economic possibility of a transfer for 18 months. I think we were the only team in the history of the Premier League with 18 months without [making a transfer].

"If a team like us, Tottenham, was fighting for titles with those above us and every year in the top four, getting to the semi-finals of Champions League without being able to do a transfer for 18 months, all because we needed to get used to the [Premier League financial controls]? They were so strict with us but also so lenient with others. Because of that, that's why I say: it's all very strange."

Manchester City's issues started when a 2018 investigation by German paper Der Spiegel showed potential financial improprieties, citing leaked internal documents, outlining a host of potential violations occurring over a 10-year span between 2008 and 2018.

City – who have always denied the allegations – were subsequently charged by the Premier League in 2023 of falsifying details of their finances, with some of those issues centering around payments to players and coaches. They have also been accused of violating Uefa's financial fair play regulations, and the Premier League's own profit and sustainability rules (PSRs).

Uefa made an attempt at disciplining City in 2020, banning the club from Uefa-sanctioned competition like the Champions League and fining them €30m. That punishment was later overturned by the court for arbitration of sport; some of the violations, they said, occurred too long ago to be punished and others weren't adequately proven.

City are widely expected to appeal against the Premier League's verdicts in the next two weeks and the ensuing legal proceedings could drag out for an extended period.

When asked what he feels a potential punishment should be, Pochettino again expressed his disappointment at the overall situation.

"Whatever punishment [they choose], it's impossible to turn back time," he said. "It's done a lot of damage, more than anything the guidelines. At the end of the day many clubs followed the rules and some didn't. Maybe they thought that the punishment [wouldn't come for a lot of years] – what are they going to do? An economic punishment? Docking points? It's really hard.

"It's sad," Pochettino continued. "It is a huge sadness. At the end of the day we get into a situation where what got celebrated wasn't that real, what seemed good maybe wasn't so good, what didn't look good maybe was good but couldn't be good because of what happened. At the end of the day, we went through something where sporting fairness didn't exist. So, how do you repair everything that was damaged because of that, if it's true all of the 114 rules that were broken, we've lived through a period of deception."

Last week, Pochettino offered his thoughts on the punishment handed down to Chelsea, who were found guilty of similar violations on a much smaller scale. Chelsea were Premier League champions in 2016-17, with Pochettino's Spurs finishing in second place. The club was later fined heavily by the Premier League for undisclosed payments to players, coaches and other involved parties. The club was also hit with a nine-month academy transfer ban.

"We should win one title, one Premier League," Pochettino told UK-based media last week. "They were punished, they admitted, so that's it? The title should be for the team that was second … It's true that we didn't compete with the same rules. OK, now we can say that they scored goals, they won games, and like this. OK, that's it, but it's completely fair to say that we didn't compete before the start of the season with the same card."

"Maybe with the same rules, if we apply the same things, maybe we could've signed some players that would have made the team better or scored more goals," said Pochettino. "It's not me complaining. It's the truth. If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second best team."

title: Donovan Mitchell didn’t think LeBron James would sign with 76ers
description: “I knew probably as much as you did.”
fullText:
CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers were hoping to land LeBron James in free agency after he announced he was leaving the Los Angeles Lakers last July. After almost a month of waiting around, he ended up choosing to end his career with the Philadelphia 76ers. A decision that he says won't result in him leaving his family just to end up getting bounced in the second round — which is pretty optimistic since the Sixers haven't advanced out of the second round since 2001.

The only people seemingly aware of what James was thinking during the free agency process were the players he was communicating with. But from the sound of things, not even those on the short list of his final destination knew much of what LeBron was thinking.

"I knew probably as much as you did," Mitchell said when asked about his thoughts on James signing with Philadelphia.

Mitchell also admitted that he thought LeBron was going to come back and end his career where it started.

"I think for a lot of reasons it made sense (for him to sign with Cleveland)," Mitchell said. "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, he'd be in Golden State."

Now James is in Philadelphia playing for one of the handful of teams that stand in the way of the Cavs and their goal of reaching the NBA Finals. Former Cavs general manager Mike Gansey drastically transformed Philadelphia's roster in a few short weeks, placing them as one of the favorites to win the conference.
