title: Eagles vs. Bears live updates, news, inactives: Case Keenum expected to start for Chicago over Tyson Bagent with Caleb Williams injured; Zach Ertz rejoins Philly
description: Follow along as the Bears host the Eagles to close out Week 3.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears will face off on "Monday Night Football" to close out Week 3 in primetime, with Chicago facing an uphill battle absent starting quarterback Caleb Williams.

After a red-hot start to the season where the Bears managed a stunning 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers, momentum came to a screeching halt as Williams went down with a hamstring injury and was carted off in Week 2. Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent suffered a concussion in his relief and has since cleared concussion protocol, but after missing a chunk of practices, veteran Case Keenum will reportedly get the start against the Eagles on Monday night.

Philadelphia hasn't had the most inspiring start to its 2026 season, either, despite their 2-0 start. Their two wins were both close ones, emerging with a mere +6-point combined point differential against the Tennessee Titans and Washington Commanders — two teams that combined for just eight total wins all of last season.

Week 2 wasn't without its own bumps and bruises for the Eagles either, losing tight end Dallas Goedert to a knee injury, while All-Pro Saquon Barkley exited with a stinger. Barkley was left off the injury report and logged two full practices on Friday and Saturday, but Goedert is expected to miss time with an MCL injury. The Eagles made a surprising move to sign 35-year-old tight end Zach Ertz to the practice squad amid Goedert's injury,

Eagles-Bears start time: 8:15 p.m. ET
Location: Soldier Field | Chicago
TV channel/live stream: ABC/ESPN

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Bears host the Eagles to close out Week 3.

The Philadelphia Eagles officially elevated Pro Bowl tight end Zach Ertz from the practice squad to the game-day roster ahead of "Monday Night Football," the team announced. He's now set to make his official return to the field with the Eagles, for whom he last played in the 2021 season prior to being traded to the Arizona Cardinals.

The 35-year-old veteran hit free agency this offseason after two seasons with the Washington Commanders. He saw his 2025 campaign end prematurely in Week 14 after suffering a torn ACL, finishing the year with a 50-504-4 stat line as the team's starting tight end. Ertz practiced for the first time with the team on Thursday, so it's unclear what kind of role fans should expect right off the bat.

title: Ex-Heat players are speeding up integration process with Bucks
description: The four players acquired by the Bucks in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade are going to be key early pieces in the team's new era.
fullText:
Jaime Jaquez Jr. is still figuring things out, months after being one of the four players – plus draft capital – packaged to the Milwaukee Bucks in the seismic trade of Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat.

Jaquez, Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakučionis and Tyler Herro have never played for an NBA franchise other than the Heat, so the trade was a shock to the system.

The transition seems to be going smoothly, however. Jaquez, a California native, has already gotten his first experience with "Midwest nice."

"I was told that you're not really in the NBA until you get traded," Jaquez said during the Bucks' media day on Sept. 28. "So this is, I guess, my welcome to the NBA, welcome to Milwaukee.

"I've been doing my best to get acclimated within the community, go around town, go to different restaurants, meet different people. Every time I take my dog on a walk, I get people, you know, walking down saying 'Go Bucks, go Bucks.'

"So I feel a lot of love here and I really appreciate the city embracing myself, Tyler, Kel'el and Kas, we're all really happy to be here and do all we can to make our mark here."

It's a little different for Herro, who grew up in the Milwaukee area, though he hasn't lived in the state since he starred at Whitnall High School.

"It's been a lot," Herro said. "I feel like I moved here (at the) beginning of September.

"And obviously when I grew up here, I spent a lot of time like in the suburbs, not really downtown. And so I've obviously seen how much the city has grown since I've been gone in the last like eight or nine years. It's a beautiful city. I love being here and just excited to start a new era of basketball.

"The organization is amazing. I've met obviously everybody now and just how they've welcomed me with open arms. I couldn't have asked for anything more. And I'm just excited to be here, help lead this new era of Bucks basketball into the right direction."

Ware chuckled when he was asked if there was a group text chain pinging messages once the quartet found out they were headed to Milwaukee.

"You have people that you already built that connection with," Ware said. "You been in the trenches with the previous team. It definitely helps for sure, 100%."

Those four players already knew each other, but they still had to integrate themselves with the Bucks' returning pieces and other newcomers

So there was an important players-only minicamp organized by Myles Turner in Austin, Texas. Then everyone arrived in Milwaukee in early September so they could get extra weeks of working together before official practices started.

"We're just continuing to working on our game, individual stuff, getting shots up," Jaquez said. "I think, more importantly, it's just getting to know one another. Getting to know one another off the court, building those relationships.

"Today (media day) is a lot of times for other teams supposed to be like the first day of school. You get to meet everybody. But it was good for us to get out there early, get to know one another, build those relationships so that when we go into training camp, it feels a lot more natural."

Turner got what he wanted out of having everyone in his home state.

"The camaraderie was great," Turner said. "Again, everybody showed up. So that was one thing I was really proud of.

"Honestly, what we got out of it was giving us a little extra time to really get to know each other. It's a new group. Some of the guys didn't really get the chance to meet each other, if you will. This was the perfect opportunity just to get some good variety before camp."

The four ex-Heat players' professionalism was one of the main reasons Bucks general manager Jon Horst acquired them.

"Each and every one of those guys were targeted," Horst said. "We wouldn't have done the trade without one of those players.

"And so we went into this having an opportunity to try to get players that not only can help us compete now, but can also grow and develop as we go forward. So they're age-appropriate, either entering their prime or at the early end of their prime. They fit a culture and a style of play that we want to really embody.

"There's a skill-set where they play on both sides of the basketball. There's positional size. And so just kind of a high-level philosophy, they absolutely check the boxes we were trying to check if we were going to do a trade."

New head coach Taylor Jenkins emphasized that he was instilling his culture, and the former Miami players are going to be a big part of that.

"It's been awesome integrating those four guys the last couple weeks and months," Jenkins said. "Just going to slowly build relationships with them one-on-one.

"They stand for everything that we're about. You're going to hear us on a repeat, talking about our culture and identity. Before we even went into the draft, we talked about what are we trying to build here and who do we want to have be a part of that. And we know this isn't going to be the final iteration of this roster, you know, years from now.

"But as Jon said, those guys were targeted, as we were looking out there to figure out what are we going to do to build the next great era of Bucks basketball. And obviously there's the basketball component, which I'll touch about, but the intangibles, the care factor, that's what I've seen from these guys. And I don't think it's just words, I think it's actions. These guys work."

Herro is the most experienced player coming from Miami, heading into his eighth NBA season, as well as the most accomplished with an NBA sixth-man award and an all-star appearance. The other three are still early in their careers, with Jaquez, Ware and Jakučionis being first-round draft picks for Miami from 2023-25.

"They're far from where they need to be as players," Jenkins said. "And that's what's exciting for us as coaches to develop those development plans for them.

"But when you talk about Tyler and Jaime, guys that can create a lot of advantages. Kas as a young guard I think showed a lot of that in his rookie season. And Kel, he's just scratching the surface of who he can be.

"And then there's the impact on defense. How can we take advantages? Is that in one-on-one defense, team defense, scout execution? I think all those guys, in what we watched on the film and as I've gotten to know them the last couple weeks, are going to be able to really adapt to what we're going to talk about, Xs and Os-wise."

title: TE Terrance Ferguson likely to miss Week 4, Colby Parkinson could too
description: The Rams may have lost two of their starting tight ends in one week.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams may be down two starting tight ends in Week 4.

Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson likely won't play against the Philadelphia Eagles next week after he sustained a medial ankle sprain in the Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos. He missed a few snaps earlier in the game before coming back in and then leaving again.

Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson sustained an AC sprain in his shoulder, but his status is unclear at the moment.

Sean McVay said TE Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and TE Terrance Ferguson a medial ankle sprain.

Ferguson likely out for this week's game at Eagles, Parkinson's status still TBD.

Losing Ferguson is big, but not having Parkinson too would deplete the Rams' deep tight end room. Ferguson has seven receptions for 63 yards and one touchdown this year. He didn't have a catch in Week 3. Parkinson, after his breakout 2025 campaign, only has three receptions for 21 scoreless yards this year.

Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen are the next men up in the Rams' tight end rotation. Higbee had his best game of the year in Week 3 with eight receptions on 11 targets for 62 yards and one touchdown. He had two catches for 12 yards in Week 1. Allen, known more as a blocking tight end, has four receptions for 39 yards on the year.

These injuries could mean more opportunities for 2026 second-round pick Max Klare. The rookie out of Ohio State has been active in back-to-back games after not being active for Week 1, but only logged six special teams snaps and zero offensive snaps this year so far. He could see more action in the Rams' multi-tight end personnel plays if Parkinson misses time, too.

title: These former Milwaukee Brewers will be suiting up in MLB playoffs
description: The 2026 MLB playoffs will feature a number of familiar faces for Milwaukee Brewers fans, including Freddy Peralta, Caleb Durbin and Josh Hader.
fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers have the best record in baseball and the best record in club history, and their reward is a relaxing five days while the wild-card series play out, beginning Tuesday. Sept. 29.

Here's a look at former Brewers who will likely get a shot in the postseason:

The former Brewers star has been special again. He finished the year with a 1.01 ERA and 26 saves in 45 innings, with 55 strikeouts, just 15 walks, one home run allowed and an absurd 0.761 WHIP. At age 32, he's still doing some of his best work.

Traded in 2021 as part of the Willy Adames package, the multi-time all-star is one of the best pitchers in baseball, with a 2.67 ERA in 30 starts this year, 174 strikeouts in 172 innings and a 0.913 WHIP, the best among qualified American League starters.

Though the long-tenured Brewers star, traded this offseason to the New York Mets, initially struggled after his deadline trade to Tampa, he's been nails ever since.

In 55 innings with the Rays, he has a 3.25 ERA with a 1.012 WHIP. He's allowed just three earned runs in his last six starts (34 innings).

Traded in the offseason, Durbin posted a 4.4 WAR season according to Baseball Reference as the Red Sox third baseman, finishing with a .710 OPS, 13 homers and 20 steals.

If those numbers don't sound eye-popping enough to register such a high WAR number (101 OPS-plus indicates he's just slightly above average), consider that Fielding Bible and Statcast both rank him as the best third baseman in the American League (13 Defensive Runs Saved and seven Outs Above Average).

He's been a key part of Boston's surge from early season malaise to clear-cut wild-card team in the American League.

Another player who went to Boston with Durbin in the deal that brought three contributors to Milwaukee, Monasterio only had a .665 OPS and six homers in 107 games, but he provided the same versatility in Boston (games at every infield position) that he did in Milwaukee.

Anthony Seigler, the third person in that deal, played in 49 games this year but closed the year on the injured list with wrist inflammation. He's taking ground balls again, but it's unclear if he'll be available for the postseason. Seigler had a .727 OPS.

It's unclear if Grisham will make the wild-card roster after he missed most of September with a right hamstring injury, although he has said he's ready to play.

The Brewers' first-round draft pick in 2015 and breakout rookie in 2019 spent his third season in New York, and his numbers declined after a huge 2025 (34 homers, .811 OPS) with 18 homers and a .703 OPS this season in 121 games.

His defense has also been below-average the past couple of years, according to the DRS and OAA metrics.

The former Milwaukee left-hander had a quality season in the Sox bullpen, posting a 3.74 ERA in 61 innings, with a 1.27 WHIP. Hudson had a 1.73 ERA in the Brewers bullpen in 2024.

He made 15 starts and had a strong 3.83 ERA in 141 innings this year with the White Sox. He pitched in just seven games last year for the Brewers after the team picked him up late in the year, with a 3.38 ERA.

The reliever posted a 3.78 ERA in 52 games and 79 innings, with a quality WHIP of 1.13.

Richards had a 3.20 ERA in 2021, acquired from Tampa Bay in the Adames trade and then sent to Toronto in the Rowdy Tellez trade.

Since pitching in Milwaukee, he's made big-league appearances for the Blue Jays, Twins, Royals, Diamondbacks, Phillies and now White Sox.

A Brewer the last two seasons, Hoskins gets an extra week to rest the back inflammation that has had him on the injured list since Aug. 19, but it's unclear if he'll be available when the Guardians begin ALDS play.

He's batting just .179 this year with a .682 OPS (13 homers in 95 games).

He wasn't a Brewer for long, traded in 2019 for Drew Pomeranz, but his career has continued quite nicely. He had a .719 OPS this year and 12 homers for Atlanta, both increases over his last couple years with Houston.

More importantly, he can play outfield or infield defense, and he's got two career Gold Gloves to show for it.

The popular ex-Brewers left-hander was dealt from the Angels at the deadline and was excellent in Atlanta, posting a 1.63 ERA in 28 innings of work. He allowed just one home run and had a WHIP of 0.882.

He appeared in three games for the Brewers in 2024 and appeared in 20 for the Braves and finished the regular season on the Atlanta roster.

He had 10 hits, including five doubles, during his 47 plate appearances, and he's capable of playing multiple outfield spots. With Lane Thomas injured, there's a real chance he gets a playoff roster spot.

Sent from the Mets to the Cubs before the deadline, the outfielder has been excellent, with an .890 OPS in 82 plate appearances.

The longtime ex-Brewer was in the organization beginning in 2012 and on the big-league roster from 2019 to 2023. He played with the Mets against the Brewers in the 2024 postseason.

He made 19 starts for the Cubs this year and appeared in 34 games overall, recording a 4.34 ERA in 137 innings (101 strikeouts, 1.328 WHIP). The Brewers pitcher in 2021, 2023 and 2024 was with the Cubs last year when they faced Milwaukee in the playoffs.

Civale, who faced the Brewers in the 2025 playoffs, had another great year for the Cubs in limited work, with a 1.72 ERA in 18 games and a 1.064 WHIP. He's not a lock to make this year's postseason roster, but don't count him out.

Jahmai Jones, Boston Red Sox. Briefly a Brewer in 2023 and then a Tiger for all of last year, he was acquired midseason and was amazing for Boston in 37 games, posting a .993 OPS with four homers and four doubles in 76 plate appearances.

Tristan Peters, Chicago White Sox. Never a Brewer but a member of the Brewers farm system and famously traded for Trevor Rosenthal in 2022, a pitcher who never appeared for the Brewers. Peters was an all-star this year and finished with 3.6 WAR, playing center field and posting a .774 OPS (12 homers, eight steals, 56 RBIs). It was a true breakout season for the 26-year-old.

Daulton Varsho, Houston Astros. The native of Marshfield (never a Brewer) appeared in the World Series last year with Toronto and was acquired at the deadline by the Astros, but he had to be placed on the injured list with wrist inflammation and may not be available in the playoffs.

Bennett Sousa, Houston Astros. He appeared in 35 games out of the bullpen for Houston and had a 6.00 ERA. He pitched in two games for Milwaukee in 2023.

AJ Blubaugh, Houston Astros. Not a Brewer, but the UW-Milwaukee alumnus had an excellent year in the bullpen, posting a 3.66 ERA in 64 games and 96 innings, with 94 strikeouts and a 1.23 WHIP.

David Fry, Cleveland Guardians. The former Brewers minor-leaguer, traded in an ill-fated deal for reliever JC Mejía, had a .677 OPS in 91 games this year, a far cry from his all-star campaign of two years ago.

Craig Yoho, Cleveland Guardians. He's flashed some of the same high-level potential that he did with the Brewers before getting traded before the deadline in the deal that brought Bo Naylor to Milwaukee. But Yoho has also been prone to blowups, including one Sept. 26 that might have been the last straw for his hopes of appearing on the playoff roster. He ended the season off the roster, getting demoted before the season finale. Yoho had a 6.87 ERA in 19 games with Cleveland.

Alex Call, Los Angeles Dodgers. Not a Brewer, but the River Falls native won a ring last year and has appeared in 88 games for the Dodgers this season, playing primarily left field, with a .655 OPS. It's unclear if he and backup catcher Ben Rortvedt (from Verona) will have a place on the postseason roster.

Drake Baldwin, Atlanta Braves. The Madison West alumnus and 2025 Rookie of the Year had a great follow-up in 2026, starting the All-Star Game and finishing with 25 homers and an .817 OPS.

Elieser Hernández, Atlanta Braves. He was a Brewer for just four games in 2024 and has bounced around a lot, but he did have a 2.25 ERA in five games for the Braves and finished the season on the active roster.

Luis Rengifo, San Diego Padres. The infielder struggled with Milwaukee in 2026 and famously hit more home runs against the Brewers (a grand slam) than with them (zero homers before he was released), part of his revitalization in San Diego (.784 OPS). But he was lost for the season when he tore his ACL and MCL in late August.

This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: These former Milwaukee Brewers will be suiting up in MLB playoffs

title: 'Abolish ICE' shirt gets fan kicked out of Q2 Stadium before Austin FC match
description: Austin FC addressed a situation from Saturday's MLS match at Q2 Stadium where a fan wearing an "Abolish ICE" shirt was removed from the venue.
fullText:
A fan wearing an "Abolish ICE" shirt to an Austin FC match Saturday was removed from Q2 Stadium.

An Instagram account showing a woman wearing the shirt and leaving the stadium features a video claiming she was "kicked out of the Q2 Stadium" for the attire. A post on social media platform Reddit also has a picture of the woman wearing the shirt inside the stadium talking to an Austin Police Department officer with the caption: "They kicked her out."

In an emailed statement to the American-Statesman, Austin FC officials said Monday the fan was removed for violating Q2's venue policy, which states, "Signs, symbols, or images displayed for commercial purposes for electioneering, campaigning or advocating for or against any candidate, political party, legislative issues or government action is prohibited."

The club stated the fan was offered a "complimentary T-shirt" to wear to remain in the stadium. Austin FC said that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was not at the stadium Saturday and has never been at Q2 Stadium.

Austin FC's full statement is as follows:

"Austin FC is committed to providing a welcoming, safe and respectful environment for all fans.

"On Saturday, we engaged in a respectful conversation with an individual who was not in compliance with Q2 Stadium policy. We provided the option of receiving a complimentary T-shirt to remain compliant with the policy or to leave the venue. The situation was handled in accordance with the venue's matchday policies.

"Despite reports to the contrary, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has not been present at Q2 Stadium during matches including last Saturday night. We can also confirm that ICE does not use Austin FC's offices or facilities."

The shirt was worn almost week after an ICE officer shot and wounded a Venezuelan delivery driver Sept. 20 in North Austin. Last year, fans expressed anti-ICE sentiments by hanging banners in the stands.

Saturday's match ended in a 3-3 draw. Austin FC is off for the next several days, until a game Oct. 10 against Nashville.

title: Infantino makes bigger cash pledge to Fifa members
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino indicates more money could be distributed to the governing body's members from its cash reserves.
fullText:
Gianni Infantino has indicated a greater amount of money could be distributed to Fifa members from its estimated £4.4bn cash reserves.

In a letter seen by BBC Sport, and sent to the governing body's six continental confederations on Monday, Fifa president Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which proposed selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, sparking a major backlash.

His letter comes after Uefa and Concacaf - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded Fifa pays $10m (£7.5m) to all 211 members from its reserves.

The proposal will be considered by the Fifa Council when they meet on 15 October.

"I will not prejudge the amount," Infantino said in the letter.

"A single figure can begin the discussion, but it cannot complete a global policy."

Infantino issued his latest defence of the failed proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup commercial rights that brought calls for his resignation, again claiming it had been intended to generate additional money for the game.

"The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable Fifa to invest 

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan, and called for an independent review of FFE.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

title: Chicago Bears take over Monday Night Football with Case Keenum expected as quarterback
description: The Bears are taking center stage on Monday Night Football.
fullText:
The Bears are taking center stage on Monday Night Football.

But they'll do it without starting quarterback Caleb Williams.

Here's what to expect from the Bears this Monday night.

With Williams sidelined by a hamstring injury, veteran Case Keenum is expected to get the start against the Eagles.

Tyson Bagent is cleared from concussion protocol and available as the backup.

Keenum hasn't played in an NFL game since December of 2023.

But ESPN's Laura Rutledge says he knows Ben Johnson's offense well.

Before the Bears take on the Eagles at Solider Field, ABC7 got an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage.

"He's been a bit of a coach player out there, player coach, however you want to put it, and now he gets his opportunity to be out there and show what he's got," Rutledge said.

Rutledge says a strong run game could give Keenum room to work.

Former Bear Israel Idonije says the veteran's best chance is to trust what got him here.

"He can't go out there and try to be Caleb Williams. You know, he's a journeyman; he's talented. He's got to go out there and play his game, control the clock, get the guys behind him, take what the defense gives him," Idonije said.

Still, excitement surrounding this team is building across Chicago, and Bears fever is spreading well beyond the city.

"Chicago is such a great city and such a great fan base and such great people in the city. They've been nothing but welcoming for me. They show out; they show support and they love their sports teams," Bears tight end Colston Loveland said.

"This is a Bears town and people love their football and people love their Bears. So, you just feel that throughout and radiating throughout the whole city," tight end Cole Kmet said.

The team is even getting the Hallmark treatment, teaming up with the Hallmark Channel for "Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story."

The new Christmas movie is out next month.

The Monday Night Football spotlight will also shine on Chicago's Latino community.

The Bears are calling the matchup against the Eagles their "Vamos Bears" game, celebrating Latino heritage and the community's deep connection to the team and the city.

Two-time Latin Grammy-nominated Mariachi Herencia de México, which got its start in Chicago, will perform the national anthem.

Then at halftime, a special live performance will trace the history and influence of Latin music in Chicago, and celebrate generations of Latino communities that have helped shape the city.

The Bears will also recognize two local high school standouts: Alison Segarra of Amundsen High School and Alejandro Gonzalez of Dundee-Crown.

They'll serve as honorary captains and head to midfield with the Bears captains for the pregame coin toss.

And fans will be part of the celebration, too, with wearable "Vamos Bears" flags handed out at the gates.

Idonije joined ABC7 Chicago Monday morning to talk about his South Loop bar's watch party.

Former Bears player Israel Idonije talked about Monday Night Football.

Doors open at The Staley at 2 p.m.

Soldier Field's parking lots open at 3:15 p.m. for tailgaters.

title: The 49ers get favorable injury news on Evans, Williams and Greenlaw
description: The San Francisco 49ers finally got some good news on the injury front, with receiver Mike Evans and left tackle Trent Williams both having a chance to play this week after being sidelined in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.  Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams should be back at practice on Thursday after leaving the game with a stinger, and Evans will be evaluated throughout the week after hurting his ribs in the first half of San Francisco's 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.  Linebacker Dre Greenlaw will also be evaluated this week after leaving the game with a bruised quadriceps.
fullText:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The San Francisco 49ers finally got some good news on the injury front, with receiver Mike Evans and left tackle Trent Williams both having a chance to play this week after being sidelined in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams should be back at practice on Thursday after leaving the game with a stinger, and Evans will be evaluated throughout the week after hurting his ribs in the first half of San Francisco's 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw will also be evaluated this week after leaving the game with a bruised quadriceps.

"It shouldn't be long-term," coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday about Evans. "We've got to see how it goes throughout the week. Guys have been in this position before, so we'll see how it goes."

There was initially more concern about Evans after he appeared to be in serious pain after being hit late in the first half. Evans is off to a strong start in his first season with San Francisco with 12 catches for 137 yards and two TDs.

Evans has helped the 49ers (3-0) get off to a fast start despite losing several key players to injuries, including fellow receivers Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson.

The Niners' offense hasn't shown any ill effects from those absences. The team has scored touchdowns on 48.2% of its possessions this season for the highest mark through three games since at least 2000.

Quarterback Brock Purdy has led the way and still has plenty of good options in tight end George Kittle, running back Christian McCaffrey and receiver Deebo Samuel thanks to a deep roster put together by Shanahan and general manager John Lynch.

"That's the standard that Kyle and John has built around (here), just the next guy up mentality," Samuel said. "From top to bottom, it is just the way we practice and the way we play the game."

Purdy's passing. Purdy once again performed at a high level, throwing four touchdown passes and posting his third straight game with a passer rating of at least 100. Purdy's 10 total touchdowns this season are tied with Steve Young (1998) and Frankie Albert (1948) for the most in franchise history through three games. He leads the NFL with a 133.1 passer rating.

Defense getting off the field. The Cardinals went 9 for 18 on third down and had two more fourth-down conversions as the San Francisco defense struggled to get off the field. Arizona had four drives of at least 12 plays. The Niners have allowed seven drives of at least 12 plays so far this season, tied for the second most through three games since 2000.

Offensive line. The Niners haven't allowed a sack all season, marking the first time a team has done that through three games since Cincinnati in 2014. While Purdy gets much of the credit with his quick decision-making and elusiveness in the pocket, the line has also fared well early in the season. This is the first time San Francisco has gone three straight games without allowing a sack since 1979.

Special teams. A few blunders in the kicking game helped Arizona get back into the game in the second half. A punt hit blocker Siran Neal in the leg, leading to a muff that set up a 28-yard touchdown drive. Eddy Pineiro missed two extra points, giving him a league-high six missed PATs since joining the 49ers last season.

DE Mykel Williams will have his 21-day practice window opened this week as he works back from knee surgery a year ago. Williams is eligible to play any time after Week 4. ... DE Romello Height (broken hand) should return this week, but DE Nick Bosa (calf) and DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle) will remain sidelined.

4 — San Francisco has had only four offensive plays go for negative yards so far this season, excluding kneel-downs, after McCaffrey and Kaelon Black each were stuffed on one run Sunday. That's the fewest negative plays through three games in at least the past 20 seasons, besting the previous mark of five held by the 2015 and '16 Raiders.

The 49ers host Denver on Sunday night in search of their fifth 4-0 start in the Super Bowl era. They made the Super Bowl three of the previous four times.

title: AI godfathers warn of runaway ‘intelligence explosion’
description:
OpenAI chief scientist also among authors of report on prospect of ‘most consequential technological development in history’
Two of the “godfathers” of modern AI and senior executives at OpenAI and Anthropic have warned governments to prepare for an AI “intelligence explosion”, which they say could be the most consequential technological development in history.
A report co-authored by the Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton and the Canadian computer scientist Yoshua Bengio, considered godfathers of modern AI for their work in the field, urges politicians to act now before there is runaway progress in the technology.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
OpenAI chief scientist also among authors of report on prospect of ‘most consequential technological development in history’

Two of the “godfathers” of modern AI and senior executives at OpenAI and Anthropic have warned governments to prepare for an AI “intelligence explosion”, which they say could be the most consequential technological development in history.

A report co-authored by the Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton and the Canadian computer scientist Yoshua Bengio, considered godfathers of modern AI for their work in the field, urges politicians to act now before there is runaway progress in the technology.

The authors say they are concerned about an “intelligence explosion”, which they describe as a “dramatic AI-driven acceleration of AI progress, compressing advances that would otherwise take years into months or less”.

The paper, titled “What if automating AI R&D triggers an intelligence explosion?”, is authored by more than 20 people including Hinton and Bengio. Other authors of the paper include Jack Clark, a co-founder of Anthropic, and Jakub Pachocki, the chief scientist at OpenAI.

Their concerns focus on the possibility of AIs being able to improve themselves without human intervention, a process known as “recursive self-improvement”. In the paper it is broadly referred to as automated AI research and development. Once AI systems reach expert-level capabilities at AI R&D, a single developer could run a workforce equivalent to “millions” of top human researchers, the paper says.

The authors say the automating of AI R&D is the most likely source of an intelligence explosion, because AIs are already contributing to improving their own technology and the resulting improved systems can be rapidly deployed once built.

“An intelligence explosion could be the most consequential technological development in human history, compressing years of progress into months or less, threatening human control over AI systems, and severely eroding checks on power within and between states, companies, and branches of government,” the paper says.

Urging governments to take action quickly, the authors say: “Once an intelligence explosion begins, the window for action may close.”

They recommended a trio of policy priorities: requiring transparent progress reports on AI-related R&D, including embedding independent auditors in companies; finding ways to constrain breakneck AI development; and preparing to adapt to an intelligence explosion.

Anthropic and OpenAI have both agreed to having independent evaluators assess their models after warning that AI development was reaching a critical pitch in terms of safety.

Anthropic says AI now produces 80% of its own code, while OpenAI uses autonomous AI agents in areas such as the training of new models.

“Preliminary evidence suggests that a software-driven intelligence explosion is possible,” the paper says, adding this would lead to the “extremely rapid development of highly capable or superhuman AI systems”.

While this could produce medical breakthroughs and technological leaps, it would bring a trio of risks: powerful systems could enable biological and cyber threats that develop faster than the measures needed to counter them; as humans become less involved in AI R&D they could lose the opportunity to control systems; states could use an intelligence explosion to convert a modest lead in areas such as cyberspace into a decisive one.

The report acknowledges these impacts are “uncertain”. For instance, a technological breakthrough could take time to implement given the need to set up supply chains for any special materials involved or to comply with regulations. AI systems could also accelerate the speed at which risks are mitigated, say the authors.

If such a breakthrough happened, the authors say, AI systems could rapidly eclipse human experts in most fields and “radically accelerate” technological progress. Preparing for this “should be an urgent priority, including at the highest levels of government leadership”.

They say governments should consider policies that address the potential for an intelligence explosion, including: requiring transparent progress reports on AI-related R&D, including embedding independent auditors in companies; limiting how fast an AI can improve in a certain time period; working with datacentres to enable pausing certain AI R&D projects; making sure automated AI R&D systems are fully isolated and cannot escape human control; creating “emergency response plans” for the various scenarios that could emerge from an intelligence explosion.

Despite some glitches shown by systems, such as disobeying instructions, R&D projects that would take humans months to carry out could be fully automated by AI by 2028. “Productivity gains from AI R&D automation have not yet reached the threshold needed to trigger an intelligence explosion, but gains from newer systems are likely approaching that threshold,” they said.

description:

fullText:
Chipmaker says new system was designed to prevent AI agents from going rogue amid incidents at top companies

Nvidia on Monday unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop artificial intelligence agents from going rogue.

The company announced a $150bn stock buyback the same day, the largest in US corporate history.

The chipmaker said that its Open Agent Safety Platform includes open source software that “sets boundaries for agents” and follows a series of revelations from top AI companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organizations.

The disclosures have sparked furious debate about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence systems, including self-improving models that some fear could race out of human control.

Nvidia executives said in a media briefing that the new system could have prevented a recent incident involving a swarm of OpenAI agents that autonomously hacked into the AI company Hugging Face.

“From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach if it was being used in frontier labs for model evaluation early on,” said Justin Boitano, the company’s vice-president of enterprise AI, referring to companies at the forefront of AI.

Nvidia also said its board approved expanding its share repurchase program by $150bn, raising the total amount to $235bn. The previous record was held by Apple with its $110bn buyback in 2024.

“Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in ​the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders,” Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, said in a statement.

Last month, Nvidia forecast about ⁠70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, reassuring investors who have questioned ​how long the AI ​spending surge can last after ​years of explosive growth.

The Hugging Face incident was a high-profile breach that inflamed safety concerns about AI, which were followed by similar rogue actions involving OpenAI’s models including breaching an Australian health department website. Anthropic and Meta have also disclosed that their AI systems hacked into other organizations on their own.

Nvidia’s software, called OpenShell, lets developers “formally verify an agent has enough authority to do its job and no more”, Boitano said.

Because it is open source, it can be “extended” to run on rival computing platforms including those from Arm and Intel.

The platform also includes a separate security layer called Sentry that runs onboard a chip to continuously monitor AI agent activity and can “intervene instantly” if the agent starts trying to move beyond its target, the company said.

“It can quarantine a suspicious agent in milliseconds,” Boitano said.

“OpenShell governs the agent’s actions, and then Sentry independently monitors and contains suspicious behavior,” Boitano said.

Nvidia said more than 100 organizations were using the platform at its launch, including Microsoft, Perplexity, Accenture and JPMorgan Chase.

The AI safety debate has divided the industry, with the heads of Anthropic and OpenAI championing a coordinated slowdown of AI development to let safety efforts catch up.

Others, including Huang, say it should be up to individual companies to make sure their models are safe for release.

Huang, during the annual Salesforce technology conference held earlier this month, characterized AI safety, including the danger of rogue agents, as an engineering problem that software developers can address.

If You Love 'American Horror Story,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next
description: If you are crazy about “American Horror Story” and need more chilling stories in your life, there’s one movie you shouldn’t sleep on.
fullText:
American Horror Story is kind of an institution, at this point. Seasons may vary in impact and the precise tone of the horror may fluctuate, but we’ve come to count on its gonzo sensibility and commitment to the bit. With its anthology approach and rotating troupe of semi-permanent actors (including Jessica Lange and Sarah Paulson), AHS has delivered plenty of twisted stories to keep you up at night. If you’ve watched them all (and the streamalike shows that offer similar chills), it’s time to dive into long-form horror on the same wavelength—starting with what might be the first (and still one of the best) horror anthologies ever made: Dead of Night.

Without Dead of Night, released in 1945, there might not be an American Horror Story. Hugely influential, the movie is regarded as one of (if not the) first horror anthology films widely released, and more than 80 years later it’s still considered one of the best. Watching it is an exercise in noting everything that the horror anthologies that followed—including AHS—have freely borrowed from it. If you love the anthology aspect of AHS, the way each season (or half-season) is a self-contained story with its own tone, visuals, and style of horror, this is the movie you should watch.

The frame story involves architect Walter Craig (Mervyn Johns), who travels to a remote cottage for a potential renovation project. When he arrives, he finds himself one of several guests—all of whom have appeared in dreams experienced by their host, Elliot Foley (Roland Culver). Craig experiences what seem like psychic visions, which prompts the guests to tell tales of supernatural experiences they’ve had, all of which are presented as apparently standalone episodes. The most famous of these is the story of a ventriloquist whose dummy, Hugo, seems to have a will of its own, but all the stories are well-made and effectively scary.

What really sets Dead of Night apart—and makes it perfect for AHS fans—is the way the guests’ tales and the frame story merge into a truly unsettling whole. The film conveys both a sense of dream logic and visceral fright that’s surprisingly powerful and modern for a film of its vintage, and AHS fans will see the clear line of inspiration that starts here and ends with Jessica Lange leading an insane asylum in “The Name Game” (among many, many other insane moments from the show). If you’re looking for a feature film that will slot into the same pleasure centers in your brain as American Horror Story, this is the one to start with. Stream Dead of Night on Kanopy, Plex, or Fawesome, or rent it on Prime Video.

Horror is addictive, and the only cure for the end of a horror movie is ... more horror movies. Here are a few more that any fan of AHS will love.

One of the more obvious points of inspiration (especially for Season Five, “Hotel”), The Shining is one of the greatest modern horror films. The combination of Stanley Kubrick’s cold perfection, Jack Nicholson’s volatility (and Shelley Duvall’s criminally underrated desperation), and Stephen King’s wild imagination (despite his reservations about Kubrick’s interpretation) results in a slow burn of insanity as an unstable alcoholic (Nicholson’s Jack Torrance) unravels while working as a winter caretaker in an enormous, haunted mountain hotel. Every scene in this film ramps up the sense of unease and terror, leading to one of the most famous final shots in film history. Rent The Shining on Prime Video.

Season 12 of American Horror Story, “Delicate,” riffs enthusiastically off of Rosemary’s Baby, and the 1968 film could be an entire season of the show itself. The tone, visuals, and story are a perfect match—you can easily imagine most of the usual actors from the AHS troupe showing up as the creepy, devil-worshipping neighbors who manipulate a young woman (Mia Farrow) into conceiving a child under what could be called ominous circumstances. Aside from being an ideal companion film to the series, it’s also a classic that every horror fan should watch (despite some serious implications around marital sexual assault and director Roman Polansky’s gross legacy). Stream Rosemary’s Baby on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

If you recall the weird whistling theme song associated with serial killer Tate Langdon in Season One, “Murder House,” you’ve already heard the theme song to this movie (you also heard it in Kill Bill: Volume 1). While not overtly gory, Twisted Nerve is a great example of simmering tension as a disturbed man with a split personality, Martin (Hywel Bennett), stalks and ingratiates himself with a young woman named Susan (Haley Mills). The film is dated in many ways (especially its enraging attitude toward Down syndrome), but as a thriller it still works gangbusters. Stream Twisted Nerve on Plex.

The moment Bloody Face shows up in the second season of American Horror Story, the connection to Tobe Hooper’s 1974 film is pretty clear—but The Texas Chainsaw Massacre reverberates throughout American Horror Story (as it does through most of the horror movies that followed it). Ostensibly based on the true crimes of Ed Gein, it follows five teenagers on a road trip as they stumble into the house where a man wearing a skin mask—the legendary Leatherface—proceeds to savagely murder most of them using a hammer and, of course, a chainsaw. The film’s sweaty, gritty style is a long way from Ryan Murphy’s slicker and more composed approach, but it’s a visceral kick of pure horror fans of the show will love (if they don’t already). Stream The Texas Chainsaw Massacre on Pluto or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

If “Coven” was your favorite season of American Horror Story, this is the film for you. Four outcast teen girls—played by Robin Tunney, Fairuza Balk, Neve Campbell, and Rachel True—discover that they can access supernatural forces, and seek to use this power to punish their enemies and improve their lives. Their spells have unintended consequences, however, and Balk’s character quickly goes power-mad as the girls turn on each other. It’s dark, but anyone who attended high school will 100% understand why things go pear-shaped so fast—and fans of AHS will find a lot to love in this story of teenage angst, rebellion, and occult horrors. Stream The Craft on Plex or rent it on Prime Video.

title: 10 Security Hacks Every Local AI User Should Know
description: You can run AI models locally without risking rogue cyberattacks.
fullText:
When you think of local AI, you might assume that running models on local hardware instead of paying for cloud-based services is the safer and more private option. That’s only partially true. When running AI locally, you maintain better control over your workflows and data. You decide whether to share your data with any third-party services, and if so, under what terms. You also don’t have to worry about data breaches and cyberattacks targeting major tech corporations. But on the other hand, you refuse the multimillion-dollar security infrastructure built by established players like OpenAI or Anthropic. Your security is now fully your responsibility, for better or worse. With that in mind, here are ten clever hacks to help you achieve better security when running AI models on your PC or a private VPS (virtual private server).

When running AI models on your personal hardware using a platform like Jan, Ollama, or LM Studio, your messages, documents, and chat history do not leave your device and aren’t sent to someone else’s cloud servers. If you’re worried about an AI company selling your data without your consent, or if you don’t want to end up with your credentials leaked in the next data breach, going local is the smart move.

That said, it isn’t foolproof. You’re still downloading the AI model files from a public database. You may also have to let the model access certain APIs so it can talk to your software or data over the public web. Finally, if you’re using a public wifi, anyone else connected to the network may be able to breach your operating system by targeting the AI. In other words, things are not as simple as people sometimes make them out to be.

Just this January, SentinelOne and Censys found 175,000 publicly exposed Ollama hosts that could be used by any attacker with an internet connection to execute code and connect to third-party services from a user’s credentials and hardware. If you want to run AI locally, you have to be very careful with where you get your models from and what they have access to. Here are some tips to help you get it right.

To run AI models on your local machine, you’ll need to use an inference engine (also called a runner) like Ollama or LM Studio, which let the model load and execute on your hardware. By default, AI runners are configured to run models on localhost (127.0.0.1 or 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1), meaning that other devices on your network or the public web can’t access it. But if you run your AI model on 0.0.0.0, that opens up access to all devices in your network. Anyone on your shared wifi can boot up your local AI setup, then use it to make changes to your hardware or steal sensitive data.

Sometimes, setup guides will suggest that you do this anyway, so that you can access your local AI model from other devices on your network, like a smartphone or laptop. It also comes up when people try to run AI models on VPS servers or Network-Attached Storage (NAS) devices. But this will put your data and workflows at risk, so if you did something to change the default server configuration of your model runner, make sure to change it back now:

On Ollama, you can do this by changing the OLLAMA_HOST variable back to 127.0.0.1.

For LM Studio, toggle off “Serve on Local Network."

If you use Jan, click the gear icon on your Hub interface to get to the Settings page. Then select Local API Server and make up an API key using an online generator like RandomKeygen.

You shouldn’t expose your AI model to your public IP address on the internet. But what if you still need to share model access to your other devices remotely? Normally, people enable port forwarding on their routers to configure access to their resources and data from a remote location. But you should never use this approach to configure remote access to AI models or runners on your local machine.

If you’re already running your AI model on 0.0.0.0, and you choose to enable port forwarding on your router on top of that, anyone on the internet can break into your local AI setup if they manage to guess your IP address. Cyber attackers often operate bot networks that routinely scan the internet for open ports on residential IPs, so you're running the risk of being targeted if you do this. A better way is to set up an encrypted tunnel using a VPN or Cloudflare ZTNA. Mesh VPNs like Tailscale are a popular choice for this, as is Cloudflare Zero Trust’s new Tunnel feature.

In May 2026, Cyera uncovered a new Ollama vulnerability that let attackers steal chunks of your data and credentials using unauthenticated API calls. The flaw, called “Bleeding Llama,” had a CVSS rating of 9.3 out of 10. At the time, it put around 300,000 publicly exposed Ollama servers at risk until it was addressed in patch version 0.17.1.

AI runners like LM Studio, Ollama, Jan, and GPT4All are still experimental and often reveal new vulnerabilities that get patched in subsequent releases. If your runner is even a few versions out of date, your server could be vulnerable to a serious attack vector that hackers can exploit. Always grab the latest release as soon as you can from the AI runner’s official website or GitHub repository.

AI models based on older deep learning models like PyTorch are often downloadable as pickle files, with extensions like .bin, .pt, or .pkl. But due to the nature of the Python pickle file format, these model files can be altered to execute malicious code as soon as you try to load them using your runner.

Back in 2025, ReversingLabs found two live model files on Hugging Face that had cleared the platform’s automated security checks even though they had an unauthorized remote access function hidden in plain sight. Now, Hugging Face’s own documentation notes pickle files as a major security risk.

To avoid data breaches or unauthorized access, you should only download LLMs that come packaged in newer file formats like .safetensor or .gguf. These file formats store your data in numerical format, which makes malicious code execution impossible as a model loads. If a particular model is only available as a .pt  or .pkl file, I’d just skip it. There are plenty of newer-version LLMs that use more secure file formats.

AI hubs like Hugging Face or ModelScope allow anyone with an internet connection to upload AI models to their website. While they have some platform-level security protocols in place, in cases like the incident discovered by ReversingLabs in 2025, newer or more sophisticated exploits can bypass these protocols and verifications very easily.

For better safety, download model files uploaded from official accounts managed by major model developers only. For example, Google, Mistral, Meta, and Qwen (Alibaba) all have separate organizational accounts with a verified badge on Hugging Face.  Verification badges indicate that a company account is really owned and administered by that company, because the uploader would have had to use an official company email address to log in and upload the model files. You can see the Advanced Security section of Hugging Face’s documentation 

Hackers like to use popular GenAI tools as a lure to get people to install malicious software. Often, they’ll set up fake websites or upload to popular app marketplaces where they can pose as official platforms. Earlier attempts focused on ChatGPT clones on lookalike websites that seemed like the real OpenAI. They would get people to download a corrupt .exe or .dmg file, which would then deliver dangerous payloads like Redline, Lumma, or the Odyssey infostealer for Mac. Similar attempts have also been used to target Android users through malicious apps uploaded to the Play Store.

But the attacks have grown more sophisticated since then and may even target obscure local AI platforms and Python packages. Attackers have gone as far as to breach official GitHub repositories and Python Package Index (PyPI) uploads. TrendAI reported one particularly disturbing instance where malicious code was inserted directly into the official PyPI package of LiteLLM, an open-source AI gateway that lets you call hundreds of LLMs from a single API. Positive Security also discovered malicious Python packages uploaded to PyPI as Deepseek lookalikes.

Make sure to verify where you’re getting your AI tools from. Your best bet is to rely on direct official sources, verified GitHub repos maintained by trusted AI vendors, and Python packages referenced directly in the source company’s official documentation.

I already covered how Python packages are corrupted to install malware as soon as you run them on your system. But it’s not just the LLM files and AI tools that you need to watch out for. When you ask AI agents to write code or execute tasks, they also install and run any packages or dependencies needed to complete that job. And because AI models are prone to hallucination, agents will often just make up package names that don’t exist. A recent study that analyzed 16 models across 576,000 code samples found that open-weight LLMs do this 21.7% of the time, while frontier AI models have a lower hallucination rate of 5.2%.

Hackers know this, hence "slopsquatting," a new attack in which bad actors register fake software packages under commonly hallucinated package names across different LLMs. These packages can run malicious code, prompt injection attacks, or infostealers as soon as your AI agent runs them on your local machine.

The best way to avoid these attacks is to limit what your AI agent can install and run without your approval. You can either choose to manually approve each software package before the model installs or runs it, or you can whitelist certain trustworthy repositories that aren’t likely to contain malware. Either way, make sure to review your model’s log to see what pip install and npm install commands it runs to avoid unauthorized installations.

Even when you run them on your local hardware, AI agents can call MCP servers, download and run files, search the web, or connect to third-party services using APIs. Moreover, they can read and write files to your local hardware and even change core operating system settings. All of these features should be enabled only with an abundance of caution based on your security profile. Carefully manage the level of access an AI agent or model runner has on your system, especially newer open-weight models that are more likely to hallucinate or have exploitable vulnerabilities.

There are multiple ways to regulate how much access an AI agent has. The first is to run your AI workflows inside a Dockerized container that can’t make direct changes to your system files. Beyond that, you can also restrict permissions by changing the default configuration of your agentic framework, like OpenClaw or Hermes. OpenClaw lets you choose between three default permission profiles, including ask, deny, and allowlist, which can be further scoped to specific workflows and services. Hermes also lets you set up a similar allowlist (whitelist) or restrict tool usage per cron job.

AI model runners like Ollama and LM Studio can support local as well as cloud-hosted models. But you can configure them to restrict network access through a single function even if you haven’t done so at the orchestration layer with Hermes or OpenClaw. You do this by binding the service to your local IP address (127.0.0.1) to prevent other devices from accessing it over your network or the public web.

When you keep your AI workflows local, your entire chat history, along with any credentials, secrets, or API tokens you may have shared with your model, exist in plain text on your local drives. If someone managed to access your device physically, they could take all of it. Apps like FileVault, BitKocker, or LUKS can encrypt your hard drive so that your chat history can’t be read in plain text without an encryption key to decode it. Use them to avoid the risk of exposure if your device is stolen or lost.

If you’re new to local AI, here are a few platforms to play around with. They offer the best accessibility for new users who aren’t familiar with the technicalities of AI engineering.

Ollama: An open-source model runner for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Large model library and a simple desktop app that most other local AI tools can plug into.

LM Studio: A polished desktop app that lets you download models from Hugging Face inside a graphical UI. It's been free for both work and personal use since July 2025.

Jan: An open-source, Apache 2.0-licensed ChatGPT alternative that runs fully offline on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

AnythingLLM Desktop: A free MIT-licensed app for chatting with your own documents locally. It's a solid pick if you want to feed PDFs and notes to a model without uploading them anywhere.

Open WebUI: A browser-based offline chat interface that can connect to Ollama and make the UI more accessible. Pair it with a mesh VPN, and your whole household can use one AI server safely.

title: Pixel Watches Are Getting Two New Health Tracking Features
description: The Google Health app will soon give you blood pressure trends and insulin resistance estimates.
fullText:
Google’s “Health Guardian” feature set is rolling out to Pixel Watches 3, 4, and 5 this week, and to Fitbit Air users “later this year.” Google says the new features will include reports on your blood pressure trends and on insulin resistance, which is a big claim for a wearable. Here’s what we know about Health Guardian, including how to set it up and what to expect.

Insulin resistance is associated with type 2 diabetes, and can be an early sign that you are heading toward pre-diabetes or diabetes. When your body’s insulin receptors stop responding as strongly to insulin, you’re more likely to have higher blood glucose.

Insulin resistance is normally measured with bloodwork. For example, your fasting glucose levels and fasting insulin are combined into a score called HOMA-IR. If you’re concerned about insulin resistance or pre-diabetes, it’s best to talk to an actual healthcare professional to find out what tests they recommend, and what to do with the results.

The insulin resistance feature coming to Google Health is, Google notes, “not intended for medical purposes” and “not a pre-screener for diabetes.”

Google published a paper describing some of the testing that went into developing its insulin resistance algorithm. In the study, the researchers had people use their own Fitbits or Pixel Watches to record a variety of metrics, including heart rate, HRV, and activity. It’s not clear from this paper exactly how the algorithm works or whether it’s likely to be useful in a general population, but apparently Google is betting on it being an interesting factor to track in your Google Health app.

Google said in a press release that Health Guardian is available for free for people who use a Pixel Watch 3, 4, or 5. Fitbit Air users will get blood pressure and insulin resistance trends “with a Google Health Premium subscription later this year.” So it’s free if you have a Pixel Watch, but not if you only have the Fitbit Air. Google Health Premium is $9.99/month.

It’s unclear what happens if you own both devices; presumably having a Pixel Watch will get you free access. In any case, other devices, including older Fitbits, do not seem to be included.

The new features are built into the 5.09 release of the Google Health app for Android, which is rolling out this week. (It seems iOS will be getting the features later. This makes sense, since iOS users wouldn’t have a Pixel Watch paired, anyway.)

According to Google, you can “set up” your blood pressure and insulin resistance tracking as soon as you get the new version of the Google Health app. A Reddit user who has gotten the update says that you can set up these features by going to the Health tab and then tapping Metabolic to set up insulin resistance tracking, Heart to set up blood pressure tracking, and Respiratory to set up sleep breathing quality.

Google says that you’ll receive your first monthly reports for these metrics on Oct. 1, and that afterwards you’ll be able to view this data in the Health tab.

To get the blood pressure report on Oct. 1, Google says you’ll need to wear the watch for five consecutive days in September. For insulin resistance, you’ll need to wear the watch for seven or more “days and nights” in September. I notice that doesn’t say consecutive days.

I haven’t gotten the new version of the app yet myself, and nobody has gotten their monthly report yet, so I’m looking forward to it as much as you are. I’ll update when I’ve had a chance to try out the new features.

fullText:
Hurricane warnings are in effect for parts of Mexico's Baja California Sur as Hurricane Polo, a Category 3 storm, heads toward the peninsula.

Polo is expected to reach the west coast of Baja California Sur on Monday, cross the peninsula Monday night and move inland over southern Sonora by early Tuesday, according to the National Hurricane Center. Forecasters said it should still be near major hurricane strength when it hits Baja.

In Hawaii, Hurricane Nolo has strengthened into a Category 4 storm with 155 mph winds and could reach Category 5 on Monday. Watches and warnings for the main Hawaiian Islands have been lifted, but a hurricane watch is now in effect for part of the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, and large waves are expected to wash over some low-lying islands.

A new tropical storm, Rachel, is forecast to stay well offshore of southern Mexico but become a hurricane on Tuesday, the NHC said. A tropical storm watch covers part of the southwestern Mexican coast, and swells will bring life-threatening surf and rip currents to the southern Mexican shoreline.

Activity in the Pacific Ocean is partly being fueled by a "supersized" El Niño climate pattern.

The Pacific has been unusually active, according to National Weather Service lead forecaster Bob Oravec, with storm activity running above average during what is already the peak of hurricane season.

El Niño affects hurricane severity in both the Atlantic and the Pacific. This year's particularly powerful El Niño conditions, which the U.N.'s World Meteorological Organization has said could become the strongest on record, have led to fewer hurricanes in the Atlantic (particularly the Caribbean) and 

Weather changes fast. Get real-time alerts for your area on the new Yahoo Weather app.

Here's the location, path and status of each of the storms:

Polo was about 125 miles southwest of Cabo San Lázaro, Mexico.

It had maximum sustained winds of 115 mph, making it a Category 3 hurricane.

It was moving north-northeast at 10 mph.

A hurricane warning is in effect for:

The west coast of Baja California Sur, from Punta Abreojos to Santa Fe

The east coast of Baja California Sur, from Loreto to Bahía San Juan Bautista

Mainland Mexico, from Bahía Kino to Huatabampito

Hurricane watches cover additional stretches of the peninsula and the mainland coast south to Topolobampo.

Hurricane conditions are expected along the west coast of Baja California Sur by late Monday afternoon, with tropical storm conditions starting in the southern part of the warning area Monday morning. Polo could bring 6 to 12 inches of rain to parts of Baja California Sur and 4 to 6 inches across southern and central Sonora, with up to 8 inches in spots. That could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides. Forecasters also warned of significant storm surge and destructive waves near the coast.

Nolo was about 400 miles southwest of Honolulu and 605 miles south-southeast of French Frigate Shoals.

It had maximum sustained winds of 155 mph, making it a Category 4 hurricane.

It was moving west-northwest at 12 mph.

A hurricane watch is in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals.

Nolo could become a Category 5 hurricane on Monday before it begins gradually weakening later in the day, the Central Pacific Hurricane Center said. It's forecast to turn northwest on Monday and north on Tuesday, staying well south and southwest of the main Hawaiian Islands as it approaches the monument.

Large waves will start reaching the monument Monday and are likely to inundate some low-lying atolls, especially from French Frigate Shoals to Nihoa. Swells will also bring life-threatening surf and rip currents to south-facing shores of the main islands over the next few days.

Rachel was about 245 miles south of Acapulco, Mexico.

It had maximum sustained winds of 45 mph.

It was moving west-northwest at 8 mph.

A tropical storm watch is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula.

Rachel is expected to stay well offshore of southern Mexico but is set to strengthen into a hurricane on Tuesday, the NHC said.

title: SpaceX's Starship rocket reaches orbit for 1st time despite failure of an engine
description:
SpaceX (SPCX) put Starship into Earth orbit for the first time on Monday and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites on board, despite an engine going out during ascent, a SpaceX representative said during the company's live broadcast.
"Payload deploy complete. All 26 @Starlink V3 satellites are in orbit," SpaceX posted on X at 9:54 a.m. ET, about half an hour after the ship began releasing them.
fullText:
SpaceX (SPCX) put Starship into Earth orbit for the first time on Monday and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites on board, despite an engine going out during ascent, a SpaceX representative said during the company's live broadcast.

"Payload deploy complete. All 26 @Starlink V3 satellites are in orbit," SpaceX posted on X at 9:54 a.m. ET, about half an hour after the ship began releasing them.

Ship 41 lost one of its six Raptor engines during ascent but finished its ascent burn and coasted on what SpaceX called a "passively safe suborbital trajectory" while engineers checked the ship's systems. At 9:11 a.m. ET, the company gave the "Go for orbit!" call.

SpaceX stock fell 2.2% on Monday, falling in sympathy with the broader tech trade.

Starship then fired a single Raptor engine for its orbital insertion burn. SpaceX said the burn put the ship "in orbit of Earth for the first time." The company had said it was targeting an orbit of about 275 kilometers. Super Heavy Booster 21 successfully separated from Starship and splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico.

Every previous Starship flight stopped short of orbit, flying suborbital paths that ended in splashdowns or, on several tests, the loss of the vehicle.

Starship's payload included 26 Starlink V3 satellites, built to fly on Starship because they are too large for Falcon 9, which is SpaceX's workhorse rocket.

SpaceX has said each V3 satellite will carry more than 1 terabit per second of downlink capacity, well above the V2 Mini satellites now in service. Starship releases them in sequence through a door in the side of the ship.

Monday's deployment marks the first time Starship has delivered an operational payload to orbit.

Starlink is SpaceX's largest business, and a working Starship is central to how the company plans to expand the network's capacity and reduce the cost of launching each satellite into orbit.

Monday's flight also comes as SpaceX is now a public company, putting the rocket program under investor scrutiny.

Shortly before launch, SpaceX posted that it is "building the infrastructure of the future, from supercomputers to Terafab to Gigasat to a new Starbase in Louisiana."

Recently, SpaceX's AI compute business has helped push the stock higher, after it dipped below $100 shortly after its IPO.
