title: Three Takeaways from Washington Football's 27-24 Loss to Minnesota
description: Washington's ugly 27-24 loss to Minnesota taught the Big Ten a lot about Jedd Fisch's Huskies.
fullText:
The Washington Huskies' Big Ten opener wasn't kind to them, as they fell to the Minnesota Golden Gophers 27-24 on Saturday night. Although the scoreboard indicates a tightly contested affair between the two teams, the play on the field showed something else.

Here are three takeaways following a disappointing performance from Jedd Fisch's team.

Entering the season, Washington's offensive line was very vocal about its aspirations for the season, including competing for the Joe Moore Award, which is given to the nation's best offensive line. Through four games, the group hasn't come anywhere close to being in that conversation, with its worst performance of the season coming on Saturday night.

The Golden Gophers recorded 7 sacks on the evening to go along with 9 tackles for loss and just 40 rushing yards allowed. The Huskies were once again unable to find any sort of success on the ground, forcing quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and the offense into obvious passing situations. Even then, the second-year starter seemed uncomfortable in the pocket for a majority of the game, in part due to the pressure he faced from a resilient Minnesota front seven.

While the Huskies' next opponent, USC, offers a "bend but don't break" defense, the offensive line hasn't shown much to be optimistic about thus far.

After giving up two touchdowns in the opening period, Ryan Walters' defense was able to hold the Golden Gophers to just 13 points for the rest of the game. The X-factor, however, was Minnesota's ability to control the clock and gain timely yardage proved pivotal throughout the second half. Junior TJ Thomas led the Gophers' rushing attack with 78 yards and averaged 7.1 yards per carry, while the team ran for 125 yards.

While the numbers don't seem staggering, Thomas broke tackles all night and put the Husky defense on its heels, as UW logged at least 11 missed tackles. Coach P.J. Fleck was able to establish his brand of football early and often after jumping out to an early 14-0 lead, winning the time-of-possession battle by over 12 minutes. In order to turn things around entering back-to-back games against ranked opponents, the Washington front seven will have to put a major emphasis on bringing ball carriers down at the first point of contact.

Another running back injury, Julian McMahan, who was spotted in a walking boot before the game, is out for the season

Injuries have plagued the Huskies throughout the early part of the season, primarily at the running back position. While the loss of Quaid Carr and Jayden Limar has certainly changed the dynamic of the offense, it was the Washington defense that showed vulnerability due to some key injuries. Starting corner Emmanuel Karnley and safety Rahshawn Clark were listed as "emergency options" entering the contest, and the Gophers' quarterback Drake Lindsey took advantage of it.

Third-year cornerback Elias Johnson was the main victim, giving up two passing touchdowns in the first quarter. While Karnley didn't see any action in the contest, Clark was the primary punt and kickoff returner, but did not play on defense. With quarterback Drake Lindsey throwing for over 200 yards and three scores, Walters' secondary surely could've used two of their key starters. While Karnley and Clark are both expected to return full-time soon, the Huskies need as many reinforcements as possible as they stare down a gauntlet of conference games.

Fisch and company will look to bounce back from the underwhelming performance, but it won't be easy, as Washington heads south to take on No. 18 USC next Saturday.

This article originally appeared on Huskies Wire: Three Takeaways from Washington Football's 27-24 Loss to Minnesota

title: ‘Watch Yo Mouth’: Colin Simmons Fires Back at CBS Analyst Over Peeing Penalty
description: Colin Simmons fired back, telling Brian Jones to "watch yo mouth," after he criticized Simmons' peeing celebration. The gesture incurred a penalty during the Texas vs Tennessee football game. The post ‘Watch Yo Mouth’: Colin Simmons Fires Back at CBS Analyst Over Peeing Penalty appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
After CBS college football analyst Brian Jones criticized Colin Simmons' controversial peeing gesture in the Texas vs Tennessee game, Simmons fired back on Instagram, telling the analyst to "watch yo mouth."

Simmons drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty with 5:08 remaining in the second quarter of the Texas vs Tennessee game on September 26. Referee Rod Tucker announced the penalty — which quickly went viral — as being for "simulating using the restroom."

Get live Longhorns stats during the game and breaking updates all week. Check out the Longhorns Football News app, now on the Apple App store and the Google Play store.

CBS Sports posted a clip of Brian Jones' analysis of Simmons on Instagram after the Texas vs Tennessee game.

Jones said about Simmons' peeing gesture: "How dumb do you have to be? You get off the field. It's 4th & 29. Yet they get a first down because of that personal foul… It's crude, it's classless, and it's vulgar. And it's not how a number one team or any team should behave."

Simmons replied with his verified Instagram account, writing: "watch yo mouth gang ion even kno who you is keep talking down on yo own color #sucka."

Heavy checked the source of Simmons' reply, and confirmed it did go back to Simmons' verified Instagram account.

Jones is is a former Longhorns player himself, who also played in the NFL for six seasons. He's now a well-regarded analyst on College Football Today.

Simmons and Jones were referencing a personal foul penalty that Simmons incurred after he sacked Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon. Following the sack, Simmons stood over Brandon and pretended to urinate on the field.

ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit called the celebration "idiotic" during the broadcast. The penalty extended Tennessee's drive instead of forcing a punt.

The comment came after Simmons made a separate post on Instagram, where he shared a screenshot from X apologizing for his actions. He shared in the Instagram story and on X: "All Glory to God 🙏 Thank you for listening to my prayers and forgive me for my actions. ♥️#5piece."

All Glory To God 🙏🏾 Thank you for listening to my prayers and forgive me for my actions. ❤️ #5piece

— Colin Simmons ☝🏾 (@ColinSimmons__) September 26, 2026

He also apologized in the post-game press conference, saying: "I do want to say I apologize for the celebration. I was definitely in the mode feeling myself. But it happens, charge it to the game."

Colin Simmons addresses his unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and apologizes for his viral celebration against Tennessee.

(via @EvanVieth) pic.twitter.com/tL8mgYzKsW

— FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) September 26, 2026

“We took him out and we addressed it. I’m not gonna give the guy a death penalty for an unsportsmanlike conduct. It has to about the team and not the look at me.”

Steve Sarkisian on Colin Simmons’ unsportsmanlike penalty call. pic.twitter.com/ZgQV7mlEst

— Eric C. Henry (@EricCHenry_) September 26, 2026

In his post-game press conference, head coach Steve Sarkisian said: "We took him out, we addressed it, and put him back in. At that point, I'm not going to give the guy a death penalty, right, over an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. We got to fix it, though. That can't continue as we move forward. As I touched on with the team in the locker room, we'll address that on Monday. What that looks like and how to control our emotions in the best way. I know guys are excited when they're making plays; the best thing you can do is celebrate with a teammate."

Meanwhile, fans had mixed reactions to Simmons' reply to Jones on Instagram. Some people supported Simmons, writing things like "keep that swagger big dawg" and "keep doing your thang man."

In a Reddit thread about the reply, college football fans were critical of Simmons' post. One person wrote, "For the record, Colin Simmons majors in Communication & Leadership at the University of Texas at Austin."

Another person wrote on Reddit, "This dude gonna drop to the second round."

Another joked, "My god he's doing everything he can to drop to the Eagles in the draft."

Want live Longhorns stats during the game and breaking updates all week long? Check out the Longhorns Football News app, now on the Apple App store and the Google Play store.

title: Jadarian Price’s fumble issues are not new
description: Jadarian Price’s fumbles to start his NFL career are a continuation of a college concern.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks have been blessed with tremendous ball security from their main running backs over the past few seasons. Kenneth Walker III never lost a fumble with the Seahawks and only had one career fumble on an actual run play, while Zach Charbonnet's next fumble will be his first.

Walker is on another team (and looking like a viable Offensive Player of the Year candidate) while Charbonnet isn't back for at least another two weeks. The Seahawks are relying on Jadarian Price to be an immediate contributor as a first-round pick. He's shown some flashes of explosive runs and an ability to be a receiving threat out of the backfield, so there's been a good helping of promising plays.

He's also put the ball on the ground twice in as many weeks.

.@ZavenCollins liked what he saw 😳#SEAvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/QHufimdBab

FUMBLE 🚨@SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RNgk2tQRjX

The second fumble was enough for the Seahawks to bench him until the two-minute drill of the first half of their 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. It might seem like tough love, but Price is a rookie and he doesn't have the same leeway as more established running backs.

"I think just as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Mike Macdonald said after the game. "So, when you come back after the initial fumble, we decide to calm it down and bring it back after the half. He's gonna be fine. He's gonna figure it out, he'll be fine."

"I made a mistake," Price said. "Just got to deal with the consequences."

Price only carried the ball two more times and had just six total touches for 21 yards. It was a day in which the Seahawks generated almost nothing on the ground, so it wasn't like Emanuel Wilson or George Holani were significantly better.

But the fumbling for Price is not a new issue. It was brought up in his final season at Notre Dame, in which he fumbled three times (losing two) on just 113 carries. All of his fumbles last year were inside the opposition 10, with C.J. Carr preventing a hat trick of red zone turnovers. That may or may not be why Seattle has been hesitant to give him the ball in goal-to-go situations.

Adding his 12 games in his final Notre Dame season, Price has five fumbles in 15 games. That's five fumbles over 141 carries, or one on every 28 attempts. In effect, that's two games worth of carries for Price. James Cook of the Buffalo Bills led all running backs in the NFL with six fumbles last season, except that's on 309 carries and he did a little thing called leading the league in rushing yards. Price hasn't quite built up that sort of equity to where the fumbles are a minor story due to terrific productivity.

This is not an indictment of the pick or an indication that this is who Price will always be. But for someone who was not the primary back at Notre Dame and hasn't even had the bulk of the carries as a pro, this is a legitimate concern until he fixes it. I trust that Price will be able to work on this as he develops, but it's a weakness in his game that opposition defenses are going to relentlessly attack. And this, never mind any pass protection concerns, might affect his workload until he earns the trust of the coaching staff.

title: LAFC fires coach Marc Dos Santos after just one win in last 10 matches
description: Los Angeles FC has fired head coach Marc Dos Santos after the club collected just one win in its last 10 matches.
fullText:
Amid a brutal run of form, Los Angeles FC has fired head coach Marc Dos Santos, the club announced on Sunday, Sept. 27.

"Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care and contributions to LAFC," John Thorrington, LAFC president of soccer operations, said in a statement. "We wish Marc and his family all the best moving forward."

An interim head coach has not yet been named by the team.

Dos Santos was in his first season as LAFC's head coach after spending five seasons as an assistant with the club (2018, 2022-25). When previous LAFC head coach Steve Cherundolo stepped aside after the 2025 season, Do Santos was elevated to the top job. The results did not meet the standards of a club that expects to compete for multiple trophies each season.

Despite a roster featuring World Cup-winning goalkeeper Hugo Lloris, South Korean soccer icon Son Heung-min and former MLS Golden Boot winner Denis Bouanga, LAFC managed just one win in its last 10 matches and dropped to sixth in the Western Conference standings.

LAFC has six matches remaining in the MLS regular season, starting with a home fixture against the Western Conference-leading Vancouver Whitecaps on Saturday, Oct. 10.

title: Grading Jameis Winston's winning performance in Giants' Week 3 victory
description: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took over the offense in Week 3 victory over Titans. Here's what we saw and how we grade his performance
fullText:
EAST RUTHERFORD - New York Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked for his assessment of Jameis Winston's performance following Sunday's 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans.

Winston got his first start of the season in the aftermath of Jaxson Dart's knee surgery, and Harbaugh turned to wisdom from the patron saint of Italy to put the quarterback's game in perspective.

"I thought Jameis did what was required in this game," Harbaugh said. "The first thing you have to do is what's necessary, what's required, [and] after that, then you can do what's possible. Then maybe the impossible becomes possible. That's from St. Francis of Assisi, in case you were wondering. I thought [Winston] did what was required. He did what was necessary."

Winston stepped right into the spotlight in Dart's absence, and here's what we saw and how we grade his performance:

At 32, Winston has been given an opportunity no one on the Giants wanted to see come about this way, Winston included. But as Harbaugh said, "The season's not over, but it is for [Dart]."

So how different would the Giants be offensively with Winston in for Dart? The approach to a power running game was going to cranked up even more, but what that would look like without the threat of Dart being a part of that on the ground was uncertain. The Giants had three backs - Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy - active against the Titans.

Winston stayed on the field and worked extra after practice in a short week working on timing not just with receivers Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney and tight end Theo Johnson, but also center John Michael Schmitz.

All of those teammates worked almost exclusively with Dart since training camp began, so there was a learning curve in terms of rapport and chemistry to speed up as fast as they can.

Winston finished 14-of-22 passing for 118 yards, and most importantly, he stayed away from making the kind of mistake that has become his calling card. All of that was a positive in the rainy and windy weather that swept through the Meadowlands for much of Sunday afternoon.

The circumstances have worked against Winston in each of his first two appearances, and that's not intended as an excuse for average to below average play. The Rams jumped on the Giants almost immediately when Dart injured his knee, and Winston spent the week working with the scout team while Dart got all the first-team reps.

In reality, the Giants knew coming into this one that they would play relatively conservatively, lean on the running game, the defense against Titans second-year QB Cam Ward and what they believed would be a significant advantage on special teams, especially with punter Jordan Stout and the coverage unit flipping the field throughout the game.

Had the weather been more favorable, the Giants would have likely leaned toward concepts that play to Winston's strengths: a power arm that can attack defenses downfield, and 

Traditionally, Winston has a quick release, delivering the ball in rhythm and space. He did not appear as comfortable and fearless as he did in two starts last season when Dart was in concussion protocol. Did that have to do with the weather? That's entirely possible.

"Really, every quarterback is really judged off if they won or lost the game," Winston said. "So, I'm grateful that I get to be judged off of a win, not a loss. And I've had games where I've thrown for 500 yards, right? And the game didn't turn out the way I wanted it to be. Any time, any day, I would rather win."

Harbaugh said Winston would start at quarterback for the Giants next Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.

"Not at all. Not at all. The plans are the plans," Harbaugh said when asked how much Winston's performance against the Titans would influence the Giants' process of adding at the position. "The opportunities that you have are the opportunities you have. No matter what, we're going to do everything we can to make our team as strong as we can based on what options we have."

Harbaugh previously said they are considering all options, including free agency and trade, and that also includes potentially signing someone from another team's practice squad. None of that has changed.

Two veterans, Jimmy Garoppolo and Josh Johnson, have been mentioned as possibilities in league circles. Garoppolo is a free agent, while the 40-year-old Johnson - who was with Harbaugh for three separate stints in Baltimore and is also a former Giant - is on the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad.

Gardner Minshew was with Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy in Kansas City, but he is on the Arizona Cardinals' active roster. Justin Fields was also with Nagy as a rookie in Chicago when the latter was the head coach. His running ability could tempt the Giants to consider sending an asset to the Chiefs, where Fields is currently the backup to Patrick Mahomes.

"Look, I am so happy and grateful that the New York Football Giants won the football game," Winston said. "Anything else that is outside of me, it is what it is. I'm grateful that we get to celebrate as a team. Played great complementary football. Our punter was amazing. Jordan did an incredible job. And I was talking to the guys in the locker room, it's a confidence that's created when you're able to win games like that. You guys have been here over the past few years. Let me ask you something, would the old New York Football Giants, would they have won those games? They said no. So, it's good when you're able to find a way to have one of those days."

Said Winston: "I think when you are presented with a situation where your defense is better than them, you do what's required for your team to win."

That, of course, is the bottom line. It's what matters more than anything else. Very little was pretty, maybe except for Jevon Holland's game-sealing interception of Cam Ward in the end zone, but things could have been much, much worse if Winston pressed the issue. He played within the game plan and deserves credit for that.

The result in the win column is reason to evaluate his showing on a curve, kicking on the surface what felt like a C- up a full letter grade.

If we're treating Sunday's outing as a one-off, Winston had a winning performance and you can't take that away from him. You can't spend all this time talking about how Winston can't turn the ball over, he doesn't and then ding him for being protective of the football.

Winston completed five passes to Malik Nabers, but no explosive plays. Isaiah Likely had just two catches on five targets for 13 yards. He ripped a beautiful strike to Darnell Mooney to move the sticks on one of the four Giants' scoring drives, setting up one of rookie Dominic Zvada's four field goals. He also had a key 15-yard scramble on one of those scoring possessions.

Yet what the Giants need to decide is whether circumstances have put Winston in tough spots (short week, lack of preparation with the first-team offense, weather), or concern over his skill set is proven to be real.

And if that's the case, the Giants won't be able to sustain success regardless. They need better QB play in the coming weeks to have a chance, no matter if that is Jameis Winston or someone else.

This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: Grading Jameis Winston's winning performance in Giants' Week 3 victory

title: Josh Allen injury scare is major concern for Buffalo Bills after Week 3
description: Josh Allen suffered a left knee injury scare in Week 3, but the initial concern points toward a contusion rather than a major tear.
fullText:
One of the NFL's Super Bowl favorites to come out of the AFC this season is unquestionably the Buffalo Bills. They have started the season red hot at 3-0, winning high-scoring games in each of their first three weeks. The key to their success? Quarterback Josh Allen.

However, Allen suffered an injury scare in Week 3 that has many Bills fans and analysts concerned about the star quarterback. In the fourth quarter, Allen took a shot to his left knee. Although he didn't leave the game, cameras captured him in clear discomfort.

MORE: Josh Allen closing in on Buffalo Bills history after second rushing touchdown

It remains unclear how serious the injury could be, but one user on X offered his opinion. The account known as "Thigh Doctor," who is also a Bills fan, provided footage of Allen during and after the game.

#billsmafia Josh Allen LEFT knee

Took helmet to knee at 9:46 in 4th. Grimaced. Did have one more designed run next drive 

Limping postgame, leaning onto right leg, painful back-step in locker room 

Contusion most likely vs MCL/meniscus pic.twitter.com/fQBpop63N8

— Thigh Doctor (@ThighDoctor) September 27, 2026

Thigh Doctor outlined his concerns in an X post: "Took helmet to knee at 9:46 in 4th. Grimaced. Did have one more designed run next drive. Limping postgame, leaning onto right leg, painful back-step in locker room. Contusion most likely vs MCL/meniscus."

The good news is that the initial belief points toward a contusion rather than a tear. Notably, Allen's leg was not fully planted on the ground at the time of impact. His foot also wasn't firmly dug into the turf, which could have resulted in a much more serious injury.

For now, there is no definitive information about Allen's status moving forward, and much of the discussion remains speculation. However, his knee is certainly something to monitor as the week progresses.

MORE: Patriots' Drake Maye loses fumble in most hilarious way possible

Allen isn't just an elite passer. He also possesses a rare combination of size and athleticism that forces defenses to account for him as a runner. He has turned numerous big runs into touchdowns throughout his career.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) makes a pass against Detroit Lions during the first half at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, NY, on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026.

A nagging knee injury could affect Allen moving forward, particularly given how much the Bills rely on his ability to make plays with his legs. However, Allen has consistently shown his toughness and ability to play through adversity.

For now, Allen and the Bills are 3-0 as they prepare to welcome the defending AFC champion New England Patriots.

title: Tulane clutches up; Will Hall gets revenge on Southern Miss, 24-21
description: Maurice Turner rushes for 200 yards, bringing in the game-winner to give Tulane the Bell.
fullText:
Tulane and Southern Miss was already an established rivalry. The Battle for the Bell dates back to 1979, and the Green Wave and Golden Eagles settled things on an annual basis from 1979 through 2006. Even though conference realignment drew the rivals apart, the teams regularly schedule each other in the non-conference slate and Saturday marked the fifth meeting since January 2020.

But this iteration was unlike previous iterations of The Battle for the Bell. Emotions were supercharged and both teams had something to prove, thanks to the programs' shared connections of Will Hall. The first-year Tulane head coach leverage his success as the Green Wave's offensive coordinator into a Southern Miss head coaching job. Hall spent 2021-24 as the Golden Eagles' frontman and even delivered a signature win over a 2022 Tulane team which finished No. 9 in the AP Poll.

However, he finished his tenure in Hattiesburg 14-30 and needed to prove he could overcome those struggles at his new program. Southern Miss nearly pulled off the upset over its former head coach, but Hall and the Green Wave prevailed on their homefield. Tulane's 10-0 run in the final nine minutes lifted it to a 24-21 victory, keeping the Bell on campus and winning its fourth matchup in the rivalry's last five installments.

The heavily favorited Tulane found itself in an adverse situation when Southern Miss possessed the ball up 21-14 in the fourth quarter. The Green Wave defense forced a punt but was unable to tie the score, settling for a 26-yard Cooper Helmke field goal with 8:35 remaining.

However, the Green Wave caught a big break when Southern Miss missed its response field goal on the other end. Two plays later, Tulane was in front for the first time in the second half. Running back Maurice Turner found daylight and sprinted toward the end zone. Two Southern Miss defenders converged toward the running back and attempted a simultaneous tackle, but Turner shed them both en route to a 74-yard go-ahead touchdown run.

That capped a 200-yard outing on the ground by Turner, who became the second Tulane running back in two home games this year to rush for 200, after Jaylin Lucas posted 212 in Week 2 against South Alabama. Turner only needed 12 carries to attain his career-high and also cashed in a breakaway 43-yard touchdown in the second quarter.

Turner's 74-yard scamper occurred with 5:26 remaining, but the clutch heroics weren't done yet. Southern Miss pushed the ball all the way to the Green Wave 3-yard line, on the doorstep of a go-ahead touchdown. A key 3rd-and-goal stop forced Southern Miss to settle for the game-tying field goal, however, Creighton Wilbanks' chip shot attempt was altered at the line of scrimmage. 6'5", 260-pound redshirt freshman defensive end Josh Lewis got a hand on it, preserving Tulane's 3-point advantage with 1:45 to go.

The Green Wave needed a first down to maintain the Bell. Facing a critical 3rd-and-5, the team placed its fate in the hands of somebody who had never recorded a stat before. Fourth-string quarterback Dagan Bruno entered the game and collected nine yards on the third down, sparking a fervent celebration and allowing Tulane to enter victory formation.

Bruno was the third different Tulane quarterback to take snaps in the fourth quarter alone. After starter Kadin Semonza threw an interception in the first minute of the final stanza, Hall made a change, inserting true freshman Trace Johnson into the contest. Johnson only completed 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards, but he quarterbacked Tulane's late 10-0 rally in his first action of the season.

Saturday night's matchup was somewhat of a paradox, considering it featured 846 yards of combined offense, yet 16 punts. Tulane did the majority of its damage on the ground with breakaway Turner runs, while Southern Miss picked apart the Tulane secondary with backup quarterback Landry Lyddy, who threw for 243 yards and three touchdowns. The Green Wave ultimately prevailed in the somewhat low-scoring affair, allowing Hall to make a statement against his former program.

Southern Miss (1-3, 0-0 Sun Belt) remains winless against FBS competition in Blake Anderson's first year at the helm. The Golden Eagles still lead the all-time series in The Battle for the Bell, 24-11, but the prize has largely been property of the Green Wave for the last decade. Anderson and the Golden Eagles now turn to a bye week, but it's not a full bye. Southern Miss returns to action Tuesday, Oct. 6 in a midweek road trip to Troy.

Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) finished its non-conference schedule at .500. The Green Wave required two home fourth quarter comebacks against Sun Belt competition for their two wins, and they hope that momentum can springboard into American play. The quest for a fifth-straight conference championship appearance officially begins in two weeks, when Tulane opens American play at Army.

title: Presidents Cup winners and losers after US completes dramatic comeback
description: Here are winners and losers from Sunday at the 2026 Presidents Cup, when the U.S. team rallied to beat the Internationals for the 11th-straight time.
fullText:
MEDINAH, IL — Xander Schauffele missed the putt and everyone started running.

Scottie Scheffler, Justin Thomas, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Collin Morikawa and the rest of the U.S. Presidents Cup team didn't want to miss the end of the Americans' dramatic comeback at Medinah Country Club on Sunday, Sept. 27. So when Schauffele failed to close his singles match against Ryan Fox on the 16th green, they all took off for the 18th green with little time to spare.

Thomas, Young and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun led the way, bolting through the crowd and weaving past gawking fans in order to be at the 18th green when U.S. teammate Jacob Bridgeman arrived with his own chance to score the winning point.

They didn't have to move again.

Facing the prospect of a humiliating defeat on home turf in an event it rarely loses, the U.S. rallied for a 17-13 win over the International team at the Presidents Cup. It was the Americans' 11th straight victory at the event, and occurred with President Donald Trump in attendance for the opening tee shots and trophy ceremony as part of his role as honorary chairman. Few felt as dicey as this one did, though, after the U.S. trailed the Internationals heading into Sunday's final session.

Here's a breakdown of the winners and losers from the final round of the 2026 Presidents Cup:

PRESIDENTS CUP: PGA Tour's major-market dilemma comes into focus at Medinah

Scheffler didn't just rebound from being benched during Saturday's foursomes to give the U.S. a crucial point in singles. He did so while exhibiting class and sportsmanship with his match against Nico Echavarria heading into its final holes.

After a fan yelled, "Go Scottie!" in the middle of Echavarria's backswing on the 14th tee, Scheffler came to his opponent's defense and shouted toward the crowd, "there's no place for that." Scheffler subsequently conceded a 32-foot putt to Echavarria (once Scheffler missed a birdie putt) to halve the hole as a gesture of good will due to the earlier distraction.

The world's No. 1 player had another uneven week in team golf and now sports a gruesome 1-8 record in foursomes matches at the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup after this week. But he nonetheless won three of his four matches at Medinah, helping fuel the U.S. comeback early on Sunday with a crucial point and a classy moment.

The Americans' first-timers delivered when it mattered most at the Presidents Cup. Rookies Chris Gotterup, Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun all won their singles matches on Sunday, with Bridgeman providing the clinching point when he beat Min Woo Lee on the 18th green to secure his first win of the competition.

Gotterup and Koivun, meanwhile, finished the event a combined 5-1-1. Gotterup teamed with Cameron Young to get two dominating victories on Saturday and may have provided the U.S. a new formidable combination for next year's Ryder Cup in Ireland. Gotterup then outlasted Christiaan Bezuidenhout in singles to give the U.S. wins in four of the first six matches as part of Sunday's comeback.

Koivun, the 21-year-old rookie, produced perhaps the most unexpected result on Sunday when he rallied on the back nine to beat Si Woo Kim in singles. Kim entered the Presidents Cup as the International team's top player, according to the world golf rankings. Koivun didn't lose a match at Medinah, burnishing his reputation as a looming force in match play events and reinforcing the belief that he could be the PGA Tour's next star.

No golfer was better than Young at the 2026 Presidents Cup based on the stats. He gained more than 10.5 strokes on the rest of the golfers who played this week at Medinah and won his final three matches of the event. Young also went out first on Sunday, turning a tied match with Ryo Hisatsune into a momentum-building point for the U.S. after winning three straight holes early in the bank nine.

Kim further solidified his reputation as one of the International team's bright stars by going 4-1 this week at Medinah. His record included a convincing win in singles over defending U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark. Kim finished Sunday as the best player on the course in terms of strokes gained for the final session. His pairing with Si Woo Kim has also given the Internationals a legitimate tandem to throw out against the Americans' best moving forward. At 24 years old, Kim's credentials suggest he'll be a cornerstone of the International team for years to come.

The International team captain deserves credit for putting his golfers in position to have a lead going into the final day of the Presidents Cup, despite entering the competition as heavy underdogs to the Americans. But Ogilvie's strategy for singles ultimately didn't work. The decision to send out most of his inexperienced golfers early didn't work out as hoped.

While the U.S. front-loaded their matches and had arguably its six best options for match play tee off first, Ogilvy sent several of his less experienced players out early. That dynamic created a wave of momentum when Young, Thomas, Scheffler and Gotterup all scored points early to put the Internationals on their heels.

The pressure mounted and the International team wilted down the stretch. Hideki Matsuyama and Min Woo Lee both lost singles matches they were winning on the back nine, with Lee's defeat clinching the U.S. win.

Scott acknowledged before the Presidents Cup began that, at 46 years old, he wasn't sure how much longer he'd be able to qualify for this event. That reality made the International team's squandered lead on Sunday particularly painful, especially since he lost a singles match to American Patrick Cantlay. This was Scott's 12th consecutive Presidents Cup appearance, tying the record set by Phil Mickelson, yet he's never been part of the winning team.

Conners lost five of the first six holes to American Justin Thomas in their singles match on Sunday and never was competitive in the third pairing to tee off. Thomas closed him out for a 5&3 win and the most lopsided result of the round and put American red on the scoreboard early to help get the U.S. comeback going. Conners was the worst putter on the course by a lot based on strokes gained, and lost more than 4.6 shots compared to everyone else on the Medinah green.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Presidents Cup winners and losers after US completes dramatic comeback

title: Matthew Stafford becomes first QB with 20K yards for two teams
description: Matthew Stafford keeps breaking records.
fullText:
With a 15-yard completion to Konata Mumpfield in the second quarter, Matthew Stafford became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for at least 20,000 yards with two different teams.

Stafford was 111 yards shy of 20,000 with the Los Angeles Rams before Week 3, and he reached the mark early in the match against the Denver Broncos. He had 190 yards at halftime, which pushed his Los Angeles total to 20,079 and his career total to 65,188.

The milestone lands six seasons into his time with the Rams. Stafford threw for 45,109 yards in 12 seasons with the Detroit Lions, along with 282 touchdowns in 165 games, after being the No. 1 overall pick in 2009. Now, with 20,000 yards and counting in Los Angeles, he owns a second franchise résumé that would stand on its own.

The two stops compare closely. In Detroit, he completed 62.6% of his passes with 282 touchdowns, 144 interceptions and an 89.9 passer rating. Entering Sunday, his Rams numbers were 65.5%, 145 touchdowns, 54 interceptions and a 98.6 rating. He averaged 273.4 yards per game with the Lions and 261.7 with the Rams.

The biggest difference is the record. Stafford went 74-90-1 as a starter in Detroit. He entered Sunday 47-29 with the Rams, and that run included a Super Bowl title.

title: Baker Mayfield dislocates thumb on throwing hand and winless Buccaneers await results of MRI
description: Harassed all day by Minnesota's menacing pass rush, Baker Mayfield fled the pocket again — this time scrambling and weaving more 20 yards backward before launching a desperation heave that was intercepted.  While X-rays didn't show a break in the right thumb, Bowles stressed the team will not know the severity of the injury until after the MRI.  Mayfield left Raymond James Stadium without speaking to the media.
fullText:
TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Harassed all day by Minnesota's menacing pass rush, Baker Mayfield fled the pocket again — this time scrambling and weaving more 20 yards backward before launching a desperation heave that was intercepted. Even worse for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the quarterback's throwing hand glanced off the arm of linebacker Blake Cashman on the follow-through.

"He's got a dislocated thumb. He's going to have an MRI (Monday) just to see exactly what inside is wrong with it," coach Todd Bowles said after Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings, which left the Bucs winless through three games for the first time since 2014.

While X-rays didn't show a break in the right thumb, Bowles stressed the team will not know the severity of the injury until after the MRI.

Mayfield left Raymond James Stadium without speaking to the media.

The Bucs have lost 10 of 12 games dating to last season and the two-time Pro Bowl selection, who has resurrected his career since joining Tampa Bay in 2023, has not played well since signing a three-year, $165 million contract extension less than a week before the season opener.

Tampa Bay's offense scored two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Cincinnati and one in a loss to Cleveland. Mayfield connected with rookie Ted Hurst III for 40-yard TD in the opening quarter Sunday, but he failed to get the Bucs into the end zone again against the Vikings.

Mayfield finished 17 of 34 for 217 yards and was sacked six times. He had an 85-yard scoring pass to Chris Godwin nullified by a holding penalty in the third quarter.

The last time the Bucs started 0-3, they went on to finish 2-14 and selected Jameis Winston with the first overall pick in the following draft.

"The funny thing is we're 0-3 and we're a game out of first place. We have to get our stuff together, reach down ... do more and figure out how we can be better," said Bowles, who entered the season on the hot seat after dropping seven of nine games following a 6-2 start in 2025.

The coach defended his decision to leave the offense on the field for the play that resulted in Mayfield's injury.

Trailing 20-16, the Bucs faced fourth-and-13 from their own 39 with just under two minutes remaining. Mayfield retreated all the way inside the Bucs 15 before launching a pass that was intercepted by linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel. Five plays later, Will Reichard kicked a 43-yard field goal to put Minnesota up by seven with 33 seconds left.

"At the end of the game, we needed the play," Bowles said of the decision to go for it on fourth down. "We would've gotten the ball back with very little time. We had to make a play."

Rookie Jalon Daniels replaced Mayfield for the final series, which ended with a fourth-down interception as time expired. If Mayfield is unable to play next Sunday, the rookie likely would make his first pro start against the Packers.

"We haven't really gotten into it yet. We'll see what the MRI says, and then we'll kind of talk amongst ourselves and kind of see," Bowles said. "But right now, Jalon would probably go in."

title: Match Awards from Germany’s 1-0 loss to Greece
description: Germany is not out for now.
fullText:
Germany are struggling in yet another tournament. The Nations League group stage began last week, where Germany drew 1-1 to Netherlands after a last-minute goal from Cody Gakpo. Now, Germany faced Greece at home and what was earlier thought to be an easy fixture for Die Mannschaft turned into a nightmare. The game featured one of the most lackluster, frustrating Germany sides seen lately.

Yes, the title of most lackluster performance has heavy competition considering the national team has been mediocre for a little less than ten (!!) years. But this truly is a new low.

Germany spent 90 minutes passing the ball to no avail, as Greece held them trapped, unable to make anything of the very ball they held onto the whole game. With 76% possession, all Germany did was progress the ball from midfield, waste an attacking chance and recycle. Recycling may be truly German, but it is better reserved for outside the pitch.

With that being said, here are the awards from Jürgen Klopp's first home loss.

Forget the goal Kourbelis scored. The 32-year-old had the most impressive defensive performance out of anyone on the pitch tonight. While every Greek player till that point mostly returned the possession back to the Germans, Kourbelis brought a much-needed pair of fresh legs and was willing to attack.

His job was simple — get the ball out of German possession and move out of the defensive block Greece created. He made seven crucial recoveries and played multiple long balls to evade pressure.

His goal too was the result of good positioning (and whatever Kimmich was doing there).

Greece brought on the right player at the right time and Germany could learn a thing or two. A defensive midfielder who can contest and win balls, retain the ball and get it past is only of that much use to a team who need the ball back like that. Kimmich played a solid game barring his involvement in the goal, but he was also not the player profile that Germany needed — they needed someone who could break past the defensive lines and find spaces to score from. Basically, Klopp will have to learn to play and adjust his game plan according to his problems.

The defenders had virtually no job in this game. Therefore the performances of Jonathan Tah and Yann Bisseck, though good, are not consequential enough to the game.

Bisseck was aggressive, fast and ready to step out to clear things — almost a bit too much on each of these aspects. In fact, his aggression resulted in an early yellow. He was playing a little too high up, but this too did not influence the result of the game. He gets the pick for Der Kaiser for a decent performance with good positioning and defensive stability. However, his need to overcorrect needs to be worked on.

Nmecha was the better of the midfield pairing tonight and he attempted to emulate his performance against Netherlands. He was trying to pick up rebounds and score off them — but looking at the scoreline, it's evident he did not do that.

What Germany needed tonight was not a player who could hold possession — they had loads of it. The Greek plan was not to disrupt Germany's possession — it was to trap them along with it. So while the ball kept rotating in the middle for almost the whole 90', Nmecha was the one trying to purpose it vertically — carrying the ball forward. He was constantly just outside the box, trying to create attacking opportunities. But it was of almost no use.

He could get the ball to Bambasé Conté but the Hoffenheim attacker himself was in a tough position — being asked to play a very specific role in his debut game. A youngster with very little first team experience was expected to break past the low block, create attacking chances, and hopefully score or set someone else up to that job. And that did not go as planned.

You cannot entirely blame Nmecha for how things went in the final third, nor can you blame Conté for his game. But Germany somehow seems to get players whose weaknesses are augmented in each other's presence. And that cost them the game.

Adeyemi continues to disappoint, but as with every other player on this list, the least disappointing gets the award. He made direct runs into the box repeatedly, threatened Greece's defensive prison and attempted to make something of the ball. But where Adeyemi went flat was in finishing.

Last game, Adeyemi did his best impression of Leroy Sané's greatest hits and tonight was no different. Mediocre finishing, questionable decision making and just plain bad luck in some instances where the keeper managed to get on the right end of his shot. Tonight he was Germany's most dangerous attacking option, yet also their most wasteful and ineffective one. However, in his defense, he at least managed to get the ball that far, and that cannot be said for the other contenders. Younes Ebnoutalib hardly had the ball, Bambasé Conté was incredibly disappointing, and Kevin Schade was near-absent.

What unlocks the Barcelona star's full potential? That remains to be identified.

The final whistle will receive the man of the match award for saving us from more misery.

Germany's biggest problems comes down to one question — what next?

Nmecha got the ball into the final third, now what next?

Adeyemi has broken past the Greek defense, now what next?

This German side has disappointed so far — what next?

These are questions — tough ones in fact, that Klopp will have to learn answers to, before Germany is eliminated from this tournament.

title: Philadelphia Union's next gear, insane comebacks & more from Matchday 28
description: While MLS-reared kids balled out for the US men’s national team in Orlando, league action continued from coast to coast as the 2026 season’s hectic final sprint rolled on, with just six weeks and ...
fullText:
While MLS-reared kids balled out for the US men's national team in Orlando, league action continued from coast to coast as the 2026 season's hectic final sprint rolled on, with just six weeks and counting until Decision Day.

If it felt like the nets were bulging around the league, you were onto something. Saturday's 13 matches averaged 3.69 goals per game, which is about half a goal more than the season average to date.

A big factor in that: Teams struggling mightily to defend their hard-earned advantage as game after game blew wide open down the stretch.

Here are a few games for which you absolutely, positively should invest, at the very least, the 11 minutes or so required to watch the extended highlights, because we can't do them justice in a couple of paragraphs. We'll start with San Diego FC at Austin FC, which remarkably was scoreless at halftime before exploding to life in the 50th minute.

That's three goals in 15 minutes in one direction, followed by three goals in 14 minutes in the other thanks mainly to the eternally underrated Christian Ramírez. In the end, the 3-3 draw was a neutral's delight, which doesn't much help either of these sides as they try to scramble into one of the Western Conference's final postseason slots.

WATCH: Austin FC rally late in six-goal thriller vs. San Diego FC

Now over to Carson, California…

Was that an epic Colorado Rapids collapse to allow a 2-0 halftime lead to fizzle into a profoundly chaotic 3-2 road loss, or a gutsy LA Galaxy comeback to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat?

Probably equal parts of both, though we'll shade it in LA's direction given the scrappy nature of all three goals scored by a side often associated with glamor rather than grit.

Having João Klauss back makes them tougher, and what a moment for Justin Haak to score his first goal in a Galaxy kit. Brute-forcing results like this will keep the Gs above the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs line.

WATCH: LA Galaxy rally for HUGE win vs. Colorado Rapids

Vancouver Whitecaps FC still lead the West. Their best performances remain the conference standard. They still have Thomas Müller, who bagged a pearler here. Yet it was striking to see them drop more points at BC Place in a wild 3-3 draw with D.C. United just a few hours after their former engine-room star Sebastian Berhalter bagged a goal and an assist for the USMNT in their 4-1 win over Peru.

With a league mark of 5W-4L-3D since the 2026 FIFA World Cup break, the 'Caps have basically fumbled away as many points as they've claimed since Berhalter was sold to English Championship heavyweights Middlesbrough. To be fair, his long-term successor Aleksa Cvetković was pretty solid in his first VWFC start Saturday, notching his first MLS assist, and plucky, shorthanded D.C. were admirably resilient far from home too.

Jesper Sørensen's current group is simply nowhere near as dominant as last season's.

Honorable mention goes to Atlanta United's eventful 2-2 draw with New York City FC, another kiss-your-sister result which exposed those teams' flaws more than it helped either team's playoff prospects.

HIGHLIGHTS: Vancouver Whitecaps FC vs. DC United | September 26, 2026

Several of the leaky teams above might take note of how FC Dallas did the polar opposite in a grinding 1-0 victory over LAFC at Toyota Stadium, Osaze Urhoghide's corner-kick header the winner on a night when both attacks were missing difference-makers like Son Heung-Min, Denis Bouanga and Petar Musa to international duty.

It's FCD's fourth win in five, hauling the North Texans up to second place in the West. Meanwhile, the Angelenos have won just one of their last 10; they've slid all the way down to sixth place. Late Sunday evening, we learned that this was the last straw for the Black & Gold's leadership: LAFC have parted ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos less than a year into his tenure.

Cavan Sullivan, Neil Pierre and Frankie Westfield are away with the USMNT. Andre Blake was captaining Jamaica's Reggae Boyz and Danley Jean Jacques was anchoring the Haiti midfield in Concacaf Nations League.

The Philadelphia Union still romped to victory at rain-soaked Subaru Park, racing out to a 4-0 lead over Orlando City on the back of Milan Iloski's hat trick, his second of the season, before the Lions clawed back a couple of late consolations for a 4-2 final score. Philly's unbeaten run now stretches to 12 consecutive matches, a club record, and also their first-ever six-game winning streak. This win nudges them five points ahead of OCSC in sixth place in the East, with fifth-place Chicago now in their sights.

"We're flying," said Iloski afterwards, going on to express his desire to earn a USMNT call-up, which is notable given North Macedonia's reputed interest in recruiting him. "It was a big game for us. We knew we were close [Orlando] in the table and we knew we had a lot of guys missing tonight. It was a big performance, a lot of guys stepped up and kept the streak going."

WATCH: Milan Iloski guides Philly to crucial win with clutch hat trick

Speaking of dominance? This weekend brought another round of the league's most statistically commonplace result in 2026: Nashville SC won in style at GEODIS Park. Toronto FC were their victims in a 2-0 result, revenge duly taken for the Reds' upset in the reverse fixture in Canada earlier this month, via a Hany Mukhtar brace, the 99th and 100th goals of his NSH career.

The Coyotes are 10 points clear of their nearest pursuers atop the overall table, and are the only team with a points-per-game average above 2 – keep that up, and the league's single-season points record, currently held by 2024 Inter Miami's 74, is theirs.

Star striker Sam Surridge ranks fifth in the MLS Golden Boot presented by Audi race with 16 goals, and Cristian Espinoza is tied for the league lead in assists (13). They are fearsome.

"It's been a really special team to be a part of," said goalkeeper Joe Willis, the former starter welcomed back to the starting XI with Brian Schwake away on USMNT duty. "The personalities that we have, the on-field technical ability and quality of the players is top; the way guys are committed to the system and the process. Everything is there for a recipe for success."

Yes, the playoffs will be a whole new ball game; they always are. But NSH are the likely Supporters' Shield winners, and they're eminently impressive.

HIGHLIGHTS: Nashville SC vs. Toronto FC | September 26, 2026

Even with star playmaker Niko Tsakiris sidelined by an injury, the San Jose Earthquakes pushed their budding unbeaten run to six, making straightforward work of Portland in a 3-1 victory at PayPal Park.

The Bay side surged ahead 3-0 before half an hour had elapsed, thanks to two goals from Preston Judd – who celebrated with a leap into the stands to 'fire the siren' – and 1g/2a from vital summer reinforcement Eduard Löwen, his first goal contributions in Quakes colors.

San Jose coach Bruce Arena is a notorious skeptic of the expected goals metric, so he may appreciate the xG battle was dead even here (1.3 xG apiece), thanks in large part to seven solid saves from veteran goalkeeper Earl Edwards Jr. Quietly, the Quakes have crept up to third place in the West.

WATCH: Löwen, Judd lead San Jose to huge win over Portland

'A six-point week for Seattle Sounders FC.'

That phrase made a welcome return to Puget Sound, where the concept had grown painfully unfamiliar to the Rave Green faithful as their team toiled along on a 13-game league winless skid this summer that ranks as one of the low points of the organization's existence.

The streak finally died with Wednesday's 2-0 home win over Real Salt Lake thanks to surgical long-range strikes from Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnák, both assisted by Paul Arriola. The resulting relief clearly fueled Saturday's 3-1 defeat of woebegone Minnesota United, where Jordan Morris bagged his 73rd career regular-season goal for SSFC to become the club's all-time leader in that department.

A quick scan of the names above tells you much of the story in Seattle – they're finally getting key contributors back out on the pitch, and their performances are duly improving. The Sounders are now back above the West's playoff line in ninth place, and thanks to a game in hand on most of their closest competitors, they're even higher on a PPG basis. Could they even emerge as an autumn dark horse?

WATCH: Record-setting Jordan Morris leads Seattle Sounders past Minnesota United

We've said it about a hundred times at this point: Whether they're thriving, troubled or somewhere in between, Inter Miami are never, ever boring. So it was again on Sunday Night Soccer presented by Continental Tire, as they scrapped contentiously with the Columbus Crew in Ohio's capital city.

When Lionel Messi hits a flawless free kick like this, positive results usually follow for the Herons:

But the hosts conjured up last-gasp drama – assisted by some sloppy goalkeeping from Rocco Ríos Novo – to set ScottsMiracle-Gro Field alight deep into injury time for a 2-1 Columbus win. Some of you may recall that Crew hero Jamal Thiaré was also the architect of Miami's stunning playoffs demise two years ago when he was with Atlanta United.

→ Three days after they enabled the end of Seattle's skid, RSL snapped their own 13-game slump, ambushing red-hot New England Revolution, 3-0, in Sandy, Utah. You won't find a better demonstration of the influence of early goals: A Revs defensive error just two minutes in served up an inviting look for Aiden Hezarkhani, allowing the hosts to soak up pressure from there on before Sergi Solans' second-half double sealed the deal.

→ Much like the Revs got a painful lesson that anything can happen in MLS, FC Cincinnati and Houston Dynamo FC got sucker-punched by the last-place teams in their respective conferences, CF Montréal and Sporting Kansas City. Upsets like these are an established stretch-run occurrence, and rest assured, other playoff chasers will fall prey in the weeks ahead.

→ Amid all the chaos we've detailed, we reckon the weekend's most 'MLSy' result unfolded at Bank of America Stadium. There, a historically dominant home team unbeaten in their previous eight games (Charlotte FC) managed to lose 1-0 to a visitor riding a six-game winless skid (Chicago Fire FC) despite the absence of Robert Lewandowski and four other Fire regulars on international duty.

Sure, CLT were missing a few of their starters, too. But with Pep Biel, Allan Saint-Maximin, Tim Ream and Kristijan Kahlina still in uniform, we did not see this one coming.

title: NFL betting, odds: Tampa Bay Buccaneers set a new record for betting futility, losing 12th straight game against the spread
description: The Bucs have failed to cover the spread in 12 straight games, a new NFL record.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed as small home underdog against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Week 3. Baker Mayfield injured his thumb in the fourth quarter and Tampa Bay lost 23-16, despite the Vikings generating only nine first downs and going 2-of-15 on third down. Minnesota also only scored one offensive touchdown.

Tampa Bay fell to 2-10 in its last 12 games dating back to last season. More significant for bettors, though, the Bucs again didn't cover the spread — the 12th straight game in which that's occurred.

The ATS loss set the NFL record for the most consecutive games a team has failed to cover the spread in the Super Bowl era. Tampa Bay surpassed the 11-game mark of spread-covering futility established by the 1983-84 Houston Oilers, per the Action Network.

The losses against the number have come in all shapes and sizes, as Tampa Bay has failed to cover in four games during the streak as an underdog, seven games at home and two as a road favorite.

The last time the Bucs won a game against the spread in Week 8 last season (Oct. 26, 2025) when Tampa Bay beat New Orleans 23-3 as a 3.5-point road favorite.

With Mayfield likely out, the Bucs opened as a 3-point home underdog against the Green Bay Packers. Rookie QB Jalon Daniels will get the start if Mayfield can't go.

title: Nets waive F Nick Pringle prior to beginning of NBA training camp
description: The Brooklyn Nets announced on Sunday that they have waived forward Nick Pringle less than one week after signing him ahead of training camp.
fullText:
The Brooklyn Nets are one day away from their Media Day and two days away from the beginning of their NBA training camp in preparation for the 2026-27 season. Brooklyn has made various additions to the roster over the course of this offseason and the stage is set for those players to compete, but the Nets are still adjusting their roster prior to camp.

The Nets announced on Sunday that they waived forward Nick Pringle, less than one week after signing him to a contract, presumably one that covered camp at the most. When Brooklyn initially announced that they signed Pringle on Sep. 21, the team also signed and waived DJ Rodman and Aaron Scott ahead of camp, implying that the team was trying to figure out who would be representing the team at the G League level as well.

While these moves could be unrelated, the Nets did sign Ben Humrichous and Dain Dainja to contracts while not providing any details on what those deals were. As of this writing, there isn't an official count on how many players Brooklyn has signed to training camp deals given that the official camp roster hasn't been released yet, but NBA teams can have 18 players on the roster at the most (15 standard contracts, 3 Two-Way deals).

Pringle, 24, spent six years playing college basketball as he began his career at Wofford before making stops at Dodge City Community College, Alabama, and South Carolina prior to playing his final year for the Razorbacks under head coach John Calipari. Pringle had the best season of his college career during the 2024-25 season when he averaged 9.5 points and 6.3 rebounds per game while shooting 57.2% from the field for the Gamecocks.

Time will tell if the Nets waiving Pringle means that he will be playing for the Long Island Nets, Brooklyn's G League team, but this could pave the way for him to get started in that direction. There will be plenty of storylines for Nets fans to watch out for as Brooklyn looks to have a significantly better season that they did in 2025-26 and it's possible that Pringle could be a part of that in some way despite his release.

The Nets announced earlier today that they have waived Nick Pringle.

title: Sean Payton handing over playcalling to Davis Webb backfiring for Broncos
description: Here's why Payton gave up playcalling in the first place.
fullText:
Sean Payton handing over playcalling to Davis Webb backfiring for Broncos originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

After an incredible 2025 season, the Denver Broncos had high hopes of making a Super Bowl run in 2026. So far in the season, though, the Broncos' offense has taken a major step back.

Bo Nix and company came out slow in Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs, and that continued the next week vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars before the offense pulled the game out late. Despite getting the first win on the board, the Broncos had their worst offensive half of the young season vs. the Los Angeles Rams.

Therefore, all eyes are on Sean Payton, who turned over playcalling to Davis Webb this season. If the Broncos offense continues to struggle, fans will only further call for Payton to take back responsibilities.

Here's why Payton gave up playcalling in the first place.

Inside Drake Maye's turnover troubles

Chargers, Texans and more teams to fall in 0-3 hole

Mike Vrabel explains why concern is 'high' for Pats

How Bills survived 5-turnover day to stay undefeated

In the offseason, Sean Payton relinquished offensive playcalling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb, marking the first time in his head coaching career that Payton would not be calling plays. While that seems stark, especially after the Broncos went 14-3 last year, Payton wanted to keep Webb as his OC and felt he was capable of doing the job.

"I think it's going to help our team and I'll do whatever it takes to support him," Payton said in February. "It's not something I would do if I didn't think it will help our team."

During training camp, Payton expanded on his faith in Webb. The head coach said that Webb's experience as a former quarterback and coach for the Bills and Giants helped prepare him for this position.

"He's had great lineage," Payton said before the season, via ESPN. "His college coach, his high school background with his father, those are gifts. Then there's his I.Q. It has come from a lot of great mentors and people, even in New York and Buffalo, that he worked with professionally...I think that's a gift. Then there's the ability and the talent."

The 31-year-old Webb is considered a future head coach, but this is the first time he has called plays in the NFL. Payton, a longtime veteran at the skill, is trying to oversee Webb's development while still aiming to win in Denver.

The Broncos offense has struggled to begin the NFL season, making Davis Webb a popular scapegoat among fans and media. That escalated in the first half of the Broncos Sunday night game vs. the Rams, when Los Angeles outgained Denver by over 200 yards at halftime.

I know Bo Nix had the ankle injury last season but Davis Webb and the Broncos HAVE to incorporate some QB run game into this Offense. Especially on short yardage, money down situations.

Payton "This is a big drive for this football game." Broncos go 3 and out, quickly. No chance Davis Webb is calling this offense much longer.

Just hard to understand why Davis Webb wants #Broncos in three-wide on third-and-2. Ends up in a sack. Need to get Bo Nix under center there.

#Broncos have five carries for 11 yards. Davis Webb forgot to write "RUN IT" on his play call sheet.

If the Broncos offense doesn't get any better, it could be a matter of time before Payton takes back playcalling from Webb.

title: Former Texas A&M stars De’Von Achane, Mike Evans hurt in Week 3
description: Miami awaits more information on Achane’s knee, while Evans will be evaluated after leaving San Francisco’s win with a rib injury.
fullText:
Two former Texas A&M playmakers left their NFL games with injuries Sunday. Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane suffered a knee injury against the Kansas City Chiefs, while San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans injured his ribs against the Arizona Cardinals. Neither returned.

Achane was involved in four of Miami's first five offensive plays before getting hurt on an 11-yard run in the first quarter. He walked to the sideline under his own power, but the Dolphins later ruled him out of their 24-10 loss. Miami had not determined the severity of the injury after the game.

Coach Jeff Hafley said the team was still gathering information and expected to know more Monday. His initial assessment was concerning

"It does not sound optimistic at this moment."

Hafley did not give a diagnosis or a timetable for Achane's return.

Evans entered San Francisco's game questionable with a hip injury but was cleared to play. He caught a 23-yard touchdown pass before suffering a separate injury in the second quarter. The 49ers ruled him out after halftime, then went on to beat Arizona 36-30.

NFL Network reported that Evans has a rib strain and will undergo a full evaluation Monday. After the game, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team was still determining whether the injury involved a rib or an oblique muscle. He did not estimate how much time Evans might miss.

For now, both teams are waiting on further medical evaluations. Achane's injury is the more worrying of the two based on his coach's comments, but it is too early to assign either former Aggie a return date.

title: Seventeen titles in five years - why Spain are a dominant force
description: We look at what's behind Spain's dominance of football with 17 titles in five years across all age groups and in the men's and women's game.
fullText:
A penalty shootout success against Korea on Sunday crowned them Under-20 Women's World Cup winners - making it an incredible 17 world and European titles from under-17 to senior level in the last five years.

Their global dominance is there for all to see.

After becoming European champions two years ago in Berlin, La Roja's men's side became world champions in the summer after beating Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final in New Jersey.

They achieved the same feat back in 2010, two years after winning Euro 2008.

Spain's latest triumph continues their remarkable dominance.

They are the first nation to be men's and women's World Cup winners at the same time - La Roja overcoming England in the Women's World Cup final in Sydney in 2023.

That's not all. The men won the Nations League in 2023 and gold at the 2024 Olympics, while the women won the Nations League in both 2024 and 2025.

"It is a dominance," Spanish football expert Guillem Balague told BBC Sport.

"It's like the perfect storm. Culturally, we do things a certain way. Everybody believes in it. The important thing is that we don't stop.

"It's another Everest because the men won the World Cup in 2010 two years after winning the Euros. Now we've done it again."

Women's football (11 titles 2022-2026)

Senior: 1 x World Cup (2023); 2 x Nations Leagues (2024, 2025).

Under-20: 2 x World Cup (2022, 2026)

Under-19: 5 x Under-19 European champions (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026).

Under-17: 1 x World Cup (2022); 1 x European champions (2024).

Men's football (5 titles 2022-2026)

Senior: 1 x World Cup (2026); 1 x European champions (2024); 1 x Nations League (2023).

Under-23: 1 x Olympic gold medal winners (2024).

Under-19: 1 x European champions (2026).

When Spain appointed Luis de la Fuente as head coach of the men's team in December 2022, few expected him to deliver the Nations League (2023), European Championship (2024) and World Cup (2026) in so short a time frame.

Spain had just been knocked out of the World Cup by Morocco in the last 16 in Qatar and the federation needed a replacement after Luis Enrique left his role.

"They went with this guy [De La Fuente] who understood the style and the system," added Balague.

"It was a very risky decision - I don't think anyone thought he would be so successful."

It appeared risky because De La Fuente took charge of Spain, who have won three of the past five men's European Championships - (2008, 2012, 2024) - without having managed a big club.

After retiring as a player in 1994, De La Fuente spent 15 years in different roles with a succession of different clubs, including managing in the lower Spanish leagues, youth roles and assistant coach positions - before he took charge of Spain's youth teams.

"De la Fuente knew most of these players from the academies and they are growing as a team," former Spain midfielder Juan Mata told BBC Sport.

"This is not only a team for the present, but also a team for the future."

Since being appointed senior boss after stints in charge of the under-19s, under-21s and at Olympic level, De La Fuente has implemented a culture of respect for their rivals, for the process and preaching patience and calmness.

"Most of you are younger than me and you need to respect experience," said the 65-year-old.

"Once we finished the game, there were footballers who said, 'coach, now what else is there to win as we have won everything in all the categories'.

"We came to the conclusion that what remains is the next match in September because this team are relentless."

The success of the national teams and Spanish coaches has spilled over to club football.

Despite Pep Guardiola's decision to leave Manchester City after 10 trophy-packed years, at least a quarter of the managers who start the 2026-27 Premier League season are Spanish.

Spain's Nations League victory against England on Saturday meant they are now unbeaten in their last 39 matches in all competitions - the longest ever run by any European or South American team in history.

Spain beat England in thriller after Kane penalty miss

Education, Barcelona & Basque culture - why Spain are dominating football

Meanwhile, the women's game in Spain has thrived in the last decade and is also starting to reel in big success in high-pressure games.

The country's victory over England three years ago in the Women's World Cup final came in just their third appearance at the tournament, having made their debut in 2015.

Spain's women then followed that up by winning back-to-back Nations Leagues in 2024 and 2025.

"The changes in women's football in Spain have been especially significant," former player Maria Garrido, who is now a journalist, told BBC Sport in 2024.

"Ten years ago, when I played for FC Barcelona, there was no La Masia [the famed academy at Barcelona] for girls. We covered our own transport costs, our parents brought us to training, and we didn't earn any money.

"But in the last five years, the situation has improved dramatically. There has been a substantial push to promote women's football, including the creation of more youth categories, better facilities and conditions, and the establishment of a dedicated football academy for girls.

"This transformation has not only revolutionised the sport but also elevated the respect for women's football in Spain."

This success for both the men's and women's teams has followed lifting numerous titles at youth level over the last decade.

The future looks bright, with many believing Spain's dominance will continue.

In Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsi, the men have two outstanding young talents who picked up their first World Cup winners' medal at the age of 19.

Vicky Lopez, who plays for the national women's team, is a three-time Champions League winner with Barcelona at the same age.

Forward Salma Paralluelo has also represented her country more than 50 times before the age of 23.

Yamal became the third-youngest player to play in a World Cup final, after Brazil's Pele in 1958 (17 years, 249 days) and Italy's Giuseppe Bergomi in 1982 (18 years and 201 days).

With Cubarsi also starting at the age of 19 years and 178 days, Spain were the first side to feature two teenagers in a single World Cup final.

"Spain have got a way of playing that no-one in the world has proven they can get anywhere near," former England goalkeeper Joe Hart told BBC Sport after their win over Argentina.

"No-one laid a glove on them at this World Cup, [they faced] just 10 shots on target against them in the whole tournament."

Meanwhile, France 1998 World Cup winner Thierry Henry told Fox Sports that Spain have the potential to dominate for years to come.

"I want to give credit to the system and what they put in place," he said.

"Because Spain never used to win like that. And now they win at every level."

title: US complete thrilling comeback to retain Presidents Cup
description: The United States complete a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup.
fullText:
The United States completed a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup.

The hosts, containing eight of the world's 11 top-ranked players, trailed by three points going into Sunday and were looking to avoid just a second defeat since the biennial competition began 32 years ago.

They dominated the singles, winning nine of the 12 matches, to seal a 17-13 win at Medinah - the scene of Team Europe's famous Ryder Cup comeback win in 2012.

Jacob Bridgeman secured the decisive point by holing a four-foot par putt at the 18th to seal a one-up win over Australia's Min Woo Lee.

There were also wins for Cameron Young, Justin Thomas, Scottie Scheffler, Chris Gotterup, Collin Morikawa, Patrick Cantlay, Xander Schauffele and Jackson Koivun.

"I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah's got a history of funny things happening," said US captain Brandt Snedeker, who was a member of the team beaten by Europe in 2012.

"All these guys fought for each other, fought for this country, fought for this team."

International captain Geoff Ogilvy said: "The US team came out firing, we knew they would.

"It was on a knife edge all day. If some of those one downs we had out there had flipped to one up, the numbers looked really good and who knows what momentum that could give."

US President Donald Trump was in attendance in his role as honorary chairman, greeting the players and making a speech before the matches got under way.

title: McNulty first US world road race winner in 33 years
description: Brandon McNulty becomes the first American winner of the men's road race world title in 33 years with a stunning victory in Montreal.
fullText:
Brandon McNulty became the first American winner of the men's road race world title in 33 years with a stunning victory in Montreal.

The 28-year-old put his hands on his head in disbelief as he crossed the line 13 seconds clear of the chasing pack, completing the gruelling 273.4km course in six hours and 17 minutes.

Australian Michael Matthews was second, with former winner Mathieu van der Poel, of the Netherlands, in third.

The last American winner of the race was Lance Armstrong in 1993.

"Until the last 800m I didn't believe, I was so tired," said McNulty.

"I'm at a loss for words. I knew something could happen but it would take a miracle and I guess today a miracle happened".

He launched an attack going into the final 30km and was 50 seconds clear going into the last lap.

McNulty visibly began to tire on the final climb and his lead was cut to just 10 seconds, but the chasing pack were unable to reel him in.

Britain's Tom Pidcock finished seventh, with Ireland's Ben Healy 10th and Remco Evenepoel of Belgium in 12th place.

Even without injured riding legend Tadej Pogacar, Montreal 2026 was still full of favourites who were expected to dictate the shape of this monumentally long race.

Van der poel, Evenepoel, Wout van Aert, Paul Seixas and Pidcock were all there, all animating and pushing to breakaway from one another under gradually yellowing Canadian maples.

But timing, not power or race craft, proved crucial.

Such was the distance all attacked far too early, and it was McNulty - a time triallist and domestique to Pogacar by trade - who took off and emptied himself.

The unassuming and, at times, seemingly timid American is a very popular winner of what was unquestionably one of the best races of a long season.
